title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Medicare Improvement Fund Payments for Seniors
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Medicare Improvement Fund Payments for Seniors The White House October 2, 2026 IMPROVING MEDICARE FOR SENIORS: Today, President Donald J. Trump announced that the federal government will be making one-time payments of $90 per person to help more than 20 million enrollees pay for their Medicare Part B premiums. Payments will be made from the Medicare Improvement Fund, which has been given $2 billion by Congress for the purposes of making improvements to the Medicare fee-for-service program, but has never before been utilized. Most eligible seniors will receive the payment in the form a direct deposit of $90 in early October. Those without direct deposit will receive a check, also sent in early October, to the mailing address they have registered with Medicare. Most Medicare Part B enrollees are eligible for the payments. Those whose premiums are already paid by Medicaid or who pay an Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount do not qualify. Seniors can call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) to check on their eligibility for the premium rebate. Beneficiaries who want to check on the status of their payment should call the Social Security Administration at 1-800-772-1213. HISTORIC ACTION TO HELP SENIOR CITIZENS: With this action, President Trump is the first President to ever use the Medicare Improvement Fund to directly lower costs for senior citizens. Established in 2008, no Administration has ever utilized or made payments from the Medicare Improvement Fund. Previous Congresses used the Medicare Improvement Fund in ways that increased healthcare costs for the American people, such as when Democrats raided $20.7 billion from the fund as part of the Unaffordable Care Act, also known as Obamacare. President Trump believes that Medicare Improvement Funds should be used to directly help people on Medicare, not special interests, and is returning healthcare dollars back into the hands of the American people to benefit them and their individual healthcare needs. LOWERING HEALTHCARE COSTS AND GIVING MONEY TO THE PEOPLE, NOT SPECIAL INTERESTS: President Trump is delivering on his promises to lower costs for American patients by putting them first and taking on the special interests that have used the status quo in Washington to raise healthcare costs for Americans. The Trump Administration is cracking down on fraud and corruption, lowering healthcare costs for Americans, and putting the American people over big health insurance companies after the Biden Administration’s mismanagement of Obamacare resulted in massive levels of fraud, higher costs for Americans, and massive profits for big health insurance companies. The Trump Administration has taken the strongest actions ever to protect the integrity of the exchanges, including ending loopholes used to fraudulently enroll individuals. In February 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to empower patients with clear, accurate, and actionable healthcare pricing information. Since then, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has ramped up enforcement against hospitals that are out of compliance with price transparency rules and strengthened price transparency rules for hospitals and insurance companies. In May 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to bring the prices Americans and taxpayers pay for prescription drugs in line with those paid by similar nations. The Trump Administration has reached 26 deals with pharmaceutical manufacturers, covering nearly 90% of the branded drug market. In his historic Working Families Tax Cuts Act, President Trump expanded access to health savings accounts for up to ten million people on Obamacare and took the most significant actions to reduce healthcare fraud and abuse in history, enabling the largest ever investment in rural healthcare – $50 billion. On September 10, 2026, President Trump announced the Working Families Obamacare Refund to send nearly 1 million Americans $500 each who had been overcharged for their Obamacare coverage by the Biden Administration. President Trump is calling on Congress to enact the Great Healthcare Plan to lower drug prices, lower insurance premiums, hold big insurance companies accountable, and maximize price transparency.

title: Marines to Support NATO Security Initiative in Baltic Sea
text: Puma Launch Marines and sailors assigned to the 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, prepare to launch an RQ-20 Puma unmanned aerial system from a combat rubber reconnaissance craft during Operation Baltic Sentry in southern Finland, Feb. 28, 2025. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.93 MB ) Credit: Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Brian Bolin Jr. VIRIN: 250228-M-UR958-9212 A specialized team of Marines deployed to Europe will be redirected to the Baltic Sea region to support the NATO -led enhanced vigilance activity Baltic Sentry. Approximately four dozen Marines assigned to the 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group, based at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, will operate alongside Finland's Coastal Brigade to provide advanced expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities. The activity is designed to enhance maritime domain awareness to protect critical undersea infrastructure and support overall security in the region. Baltic Sentry represents a highly integrated collective defense effort. European allies lead the effort under Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum and Allied Maritime Command, with the U.S. Marine Corps serving in a supportive, enabling capacity. Baltic Partnerships Finnish Navy sailors observe U.S. Marines and sailors assigned to the 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, operating an RQ-20 Puma unmanned aerial system from a combat rubber reconnaissance craft during Operation Baltic Sentry in southern Finland, Feb. 28, 2025. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.62 MB ) Credit: Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Brian Bolin Jr. VIRIN: 250228-M-UR958-8604 Marine Corps Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley, U.S. Marine Corps Forces, Europe and Africa commander, said the operational design is a premier example of European allies spearheading regional maritime security while the U.S. projects highly specialized, agile force multipliers. "Our participation in Baltic Sentry demonstrates the dynamic agility of the Marine Corps to rapidly project specialized capabilities where they are most effective," he said. "Working side by side with our Finnish allies strengthens our collective readiness, ensuring we can operate seamlessly as a cohesive, lethal team to deter hybrid threats in the Baltic littoral." The rotation will leverage the unique capabilities of reconnaissance Marines, including small unmanned aerial systems and littoral sensors, to feed vital data directly into the shared NATO common operational picture. {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} - {{slideCaption}} Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( {{filesize}} ) Credit: {{photographer}} VIRIN: {{virin}} {{slideNumber}} of {{numSlides}} {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideTitle}} - {{slideCaption}} {{slideInfo.slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideInfo.slideTitle}} - {{slideInfo.slideCaption}} "The experience, skills and systems of the U.S. Marine Corps are perfectly suited for supplementing our situation picture and supporting our monitoring of the Baltic Sea," said Finnish Navy Capt. Johan Tillander, Finland Navy Command chief of operations. Maintaining stability along Europe's critical maritime choke points protects the physical and economic security of the transatlantic community. As a defensive vigilance activity, Baltic Sentry underscores the alliance's immediate readiness, technological adaptability, and collective resolve to deter and decisively defeat any threat to regional stability. title: Kentucky Guardsmen Sharpen Capabilities Alongside NATO Partners
text: Ocean Rescue U.S. Air Force pararescuemen assigned to the Kentucky Air National Guard's 123rd Special Tactics Squadron jump from a C-130J Super Hercules aircraft into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Scotland Aug. 18, 2026. The airmen are conducting open-ocean rescue training with members of the Kentucky Guard’s 165th Airlift Squadron and the British Royal Navy's 814 Naval Air Squadron. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.41 MB ) Credit: Dale Greer, Air Force VIRIN: 260818-Z-VT419-9059 Airmen assigned to the Kentucky Air National Guard enhanced their global capabilities while training alongside NATO partners from the United Kingdom and Canada in Scotland this summer. The guardsmen deployed four C-130J Super Hercules aircraft, 62,000 pounds of equipment and 60 personnel to Glasgow Prestwick Airport in South Ayrshire, Scotland, Aug. 14-22. While there, they conducted specialized fueling operations, low-level formation flying and rapid-reaction aircraft launches to maintain combat mission certifications. The airmen also completed maritime equipment and personnel airdrops, including two open-ocean rescue scenarios with a helicopter unit assigned to the British Royal Navy. "The deployment was designed to accomplish a large amount of C-130J continuation and tactical training while taking advantage of an unfamiliar overseas operating environment and opportunities to work directly with allied partners," said Air Force Lt. Col. Nick Reinke, the mission commander and a C-130 pilot assigned to the 165th Airlift Squadron. He added that while many of the individual training events could be conducted in the U.S., it is much harder to reproduce an unfamiliar environment. Super Hercules A U.S. Air Force C-130J Super Hercules aircraft assigned to the Kentucky Air National Guard's 165th Airlift Squadron flies a low-level sortie as part of a five-ship formation along the coast of Scotland Aug. 19, 2026. The unit is supporting a weeklong joint training exercise with the Kentucky Air Guard's 123rd Special Tactics Squadron and the British Royal Navy's 814th Naval Air Squadron. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.53 MB ) Credit: Dale Greer, Air Force VIRIN: 260819-Z-VT419-9732 "At home station, crews know the airspace, air traffic control procedures, airfields, support agencies and local practices," Reinke said. "In Scotland, even something as routine as a proficiency circuit required crews to understand and coordinate with a different [air traffic control] system." Reinke said coordination with host nation agencies was critical to the exercise's success. "That forces crews to solve the kinds of interoperability, communication, planning and adaptation problems they encounter when operating globally. Worldwide capability is more than simply being able to fly across the Atlantic. It means arriving with the people and equipment needed to operate, understanding an unfamiliar airspace and support structure, integrating with allied forces, adapting when weather or circumstances change the plan, and continuing to accomplish the mission." Reinke added that the deployment also underscored the importance of relationships. The Kentucky unit, based in Louisville, worked closely with civilian support agencies at Glasgow Prestwick Airport to complete specialized fueling operations, during which a C-130J was refueled while its engines were still running. Reinke said this "hot pit" method validated the airport's ability to support the technique and provided practical experience to host-nation fuel personnel. "That partnership leaves behind a more capable location for follow-on and allied forces in the future, rather than the benefit ending when our deployment ended," he noted. One of the deployment's key accomplishments was a five-ship formation flight, conducted with four Kentucky aircraft and one C-130J from the Royal Canadian Air Force. "The Canadian aircraft commander was actually a U.S. Marine Corps exchange pilot," Reinke said. "That meant our mission planning and briefing had to reconcile U.S. Air Force, Royal Canadian Air Force and U.S. Marine Corps procedures and terminology to make sure everyone had the same understanding before execution. That is exactly the kind of interoperability that is difficult to simulate." Mission Lands A U.S. Air Force C-130J Super Hercules aircraft assigned to the Kentucky Air National Guard's 165th Airlift Squadron lands at Glasgow Prestwick Airport in Prestwick, Scotland, after completing a five-ship formation flight along the coast of Scotland Aug. 19, 2026. The unit is supporting a weeklong joint training exercise in conjunction with the Kentucky Air Guard's 123rd Special Tactics Squadron and the British Royal Navy's 814th Naval Air Squadron. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.4 MB ) Credit: Dale Greer, Air Force VIRIN: 260819-Z-VT419-9269 The deployment's other main focus was open-ocean rescue. The scenario required a U.S. Air Force C-130 crew to locate a stranded airman floating in a life raft on the Atlantic Ocean, miles from shore. Loadmasters then airdropped an inflatable motorboat near the victim, and three special tactics airmen used precision jumpmaster techniques to parachute into the ocean, deploy the boat and provide first aid. Once complete, they coordinated with the Royal Navy's 814 Naval Air Squadron to execute helicopter hoist operations and extract the victim as the C-130 provided overwatch. "The integration with the Royal Navy was one of the highlights of the exercise," Reinke said. "It allowed our pararescue personnel and C-130J crews to integrate fixed-wing airdrop, maritime rescue, rotary-wing insertion and recovery, and on-scene command and control with a NATO partner." A pararescue flight chief for the special tactics team described the operating environment in Scotland as "vastly different" from training locations in the United States. "It's a lot colder here, and the salt water is an unusual factor for us," he said. "The Royal Navy also uses different geolocation methods, and they have different tactics and techniques than we typically employ." He noted that the Royal Navy's helicopter, a Merlin Mk2, generates substantially more rotor wash than the UH-60 Black Hawk. "Those are the kinds of things you don't anticipate, but we were able to work through them and figure out what worked best for their guys and for us," the airman said. "We had to be flexible on the spot to get the mission done." Royal Navy Capt. James Hall said the exercise provided valuable opportunities for the Merlin Mk2 force to enhance capabilities outside of its normal role in antisubmarine warfare. Inspection Watch U.S. Air Force Tech. Sgt. Michael Newton, a loadmaster assigned to the Kentucky Air National Guard's 165th Airlift Squadron, observes the preflight inspection of a C-130J Super Hercules aircraft at Glasgow Prestwick Airport in Prestwick, Scotland, Aug. 19, 2026. The aircraft is one of four deployed from Kentucky for a weeklong joint field training exercise with members of the British Royal Navy and the Canadian Royal Air Force. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.57 MB ) Credit: Dale Greer, Air Force VIRIN: 260819-Z-VT419-9062 "Exercises such as this, conducted alongside our United States Air Force partners, enable our crews to maintain and enhance critical search and rescue skills, while strengthening the interoperability that underpins NATO's collective security," he said. Royal Navy Lt. S. Cass, a flight commander assigned to the 814 Naval Air Squadron, agreed, adding that he hopes to continue working with "our friends across the pond" in the years to come. Reinke called the deployment an unqualified success, not necessarily for any single event but for the readiness training they were able to layer into one exercise. "We were able to use legitimate flight training requirements to generate maximum value, ensuring worldwide readiness while working with our international partners," he said. "We also were able to build strong human relationships with the men and women of our partner nations, laying the kind of foundation that makes coalition operations successful." Spotlight: NATO

title: Adobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom partner with First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together
text: Office of the First Lady Adobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom partner with First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together The White House September 30, 2026 First Lady Melania Trump secured six new private-sector technology partnerships for Fostering the Future Together, including Adobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom. “When I established Fostering the Future Together, the mission was clear: empower children through technology and education. Delivering on that mission demands alliances between best-in-class innovators and global leaders, especially as super intelligence transforms how the next generation learns,” said First Lady Melania Trump. Combined, the new technology partners committed more than $23 million towards education, tools, and expertise, for children across the globe. Google committed $4 million to expand its SI Educator Series globally through its new Fostering the Future Together partnership. “Google is proud to support First Lady Melania Trump’s vital effort,” said Google’s Maggie Johnson. “This investment demonstrates our belief in keeping educators in the lead.” Intel will deploy its technology across ten countries through its SI for Citizens Program, SI for Youth Program, and Semiconductor Education Pathways Program. Adobe will provide students worldwide with free SI-powered study and creation tools through Student Spaces. Amazon will expand free access to its Kiro SI coding assistant, reaching 5 million students through 132 universities, while AWS Academy will provide free training to more than 2 million students. Zoom Cares will provide $2.75 million in SI for Good grants across Europe, Africa, Latin America, and the Asia-Pacific region. “I deeply value the commitment of these technology companies and welcome them to the Fostering the Future Together movement as we scale across continents,” said First Lady Melania Trump. About Fostering the Future Together: Fostering the Future Together is a global coalition of nations unified to empower children through technology and education. First Lady Melania Trump announced Fostering the Future Together during the 80th United Nations General Assembly. In spring 2026, she convened the initiative’s two-day meeting in Washington DC, bringing together First Spouses and technology-sector leaders at the United Sates Department of State. The gathering culminated at the White House, where the First Lady welcomed the largest assembly of First Spouses ever convened there for diplomatic purposes in U.S. history. During the 81st United Nations General Assembly, First Lady Melania Trump unveiled several new 2026 Fostering the Future Together regional events, including the G20 (USA), the ASEAN Conference (Philippines), Europe (Poland), and the Caribbean (Saint Kitts and Nevis).

title: War Department Prepares to Protect Election From Foreign Interference
text: In less than five weeks, Americans will head to the polls for the U.S. midterm elections. Voting Assistance A guidebook sits on a decorated table during the Federal Voting Assistance Program workshop at Peterson Space Force Base, Colo., June 3, 2026. The workshop equipped unit voting assistance officers with the necessary tools and knowledge to help service members and their families successfully navigate the absentee voting process. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.98 MB ) Credit: Air Force Staff Sgt. Jaime Sanchez VIRIN: 260603-X-IL270-8006 Every seat in the U.S. House of Representatives and a third of U.S. Senate seats, some 470 contests in all, will be decided Nov. 3, and the War Department will help ensure foreign actors don't meddle in those elections. "As we approach this election cycle, we must prove that we can and will protect the integrity of our democratic processes from any threat," said Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. "In my role as secretary of war, the Department of War will effectively wield its capabilities to protect and uphold the reliability of America's voting mechanisms against external manipulation and disruption from foreign actors, while maintaining the fundamental freedoms that characterize our country." In a memorandum published yesterday , Hegseth outlined the department's capabilities he activated to ensure the integrity of the upcoming election. U.S. Cyber Command, along with agencies such as the National Security Agency, the Defense Intelligence Agency and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, will use their intelligence and cyber capabilities to ensure foreign actors do not interfere with the U.S. democratic process. "U.S. Cyber Command and the National Security Agency are closely partnered to identify and defend against cyber threats to our nation," said Army Gen. Joshua M. Rudd, Cybercom commander and National Security Agency director. "The command and the agency regularly counter actions by malicious foreign cyber actors, including those with the intent to interfere with our democratic process." The secretary also directed the defense intelligence enterprise to collect information on foreign threats to U.S. elections, analyze it and produce useful guidance based on those findings. Finally, he directed Cybercom to work alongside the Department of Homeland Security to counter any potential cyber threats from foreign actors targeting U.S. elections. Election Guide Federal Voting Assistance Program materials are available for service members during a workshop at Joint Base Charleston, S.C., April 1, 2026. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 675.84 KB ) Credit: Air Force Airman 1st Class Nahaku Takahashi VIRIN: 260401-F-RS563-1015 "We have very important elections coming up. We want those elections to be honest," President Donald J. Trump told Americans during a July 16 address to the nation. "You can't have a great country without free and fair elections." Hegseth said the War Department would play a critical role in ensuring that happens. "Our nation's ability to conduct free and fair elections is a steadfast principle of our democracy. Assuring and protecting this ability is a no-fail mission and the DOW will do its part in supporting this whole-of-government effort," Hegseth said. "In America, the people rule, and we must ensure that their voice remains sovereign, secure and entirely undiluted." News Release: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth Signs Directive to Defend 2026 Elections From Foreign Threats Publication: Countering Foreign Threats to 2026 Elections

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Advances a Fair and Reciprocal Relationship with China While Hosting Historic State Visit
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Advances a Fair and Reciprocal Relationship with China While Hosting Historic State Visit The White House September 25, 2026 DELIVERING FOR AMERICANS: This week, President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump hosted President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan of the People’s Republic of China for a reciprocal State Visit. During the visit, President Trump advanced the U.S.-China relationship and put the American people first. The United States welcomed China’s scheduling of orphines, a class of deadly drugs. The United States also noted China’s new export controls on two fentanyl precursor chemicals, while strongly encouraging the permanent scheduling of these and other substances and chemicals to help stem the flow of illicit precursors to dangerous narcoterrorists in North America. In August 2026, acting on information from U.S. law enforcement, China arrested 21 Chinese citizens for the manufacture and distribution of precursor chemicals to illicit drug producers in North America. The United States strongly encouraged maximum sentences, including the death penalty where applicable. President Trump urged President Xi to increase production of refined petroleum products to stabilize global supply. The United States welcomes the arrival of two giant pandas, leased by China to the Atlanta Zoo. OPERATIONALIZING THE BOARDS OF TRADE AND INVESTMENT : This week, the two leaders operationalized the cornerstone government-to-government mechanisms of the U.S.-China Board of Trade and the U.S.-China Board of Investment, which were chartered during the May 2026 Summit in Beijing. Under the Board of Trade, the two countries reached consensus on recommendations for more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction. The Board of Trade also launched a working group focused on addressing market access barriers in the agricultural sector. For U.S. exports, the goods include agricultural goods, fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. For U.S. imports, the goods include consumer products such as small appliances, toys, holiday decorations, and children’s car seats. Following President Trump’s revival of the U.S. coal industry, China will import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States in 2027 and again 2028. The two countries established the Board of Investment. The mission of the Board of Investment is to discuss potential investment opportunities and investment-related impediments and to provide a structured channel for the two sides to address commercially meaningful investment-related issues. The United States and China continue to work on U.S. concerns regarding supply chain shortages related to rare earths and other critical minerals, with the goal of ensuring shipment levels return to appropriate levels. MAKING THE WORLD SAFER FOR AMERICANS: President Trump and President Xi discussed fostering peace and prosperity to enhance confidence for businesses and consumers around the world. The two countries agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity. The two countries will support each other as respective hosts of G20 and APEC, with both leaders intending to attend each other’s Summit. The two leaders discussed on-going global concerns, including Russia, North Korea, and Iran. They agreed that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon and that no country or institution can be allowed to impose tolls on international waterways. The two leaders recalled that United States and China were allies in World War II and fought side by side to win the war. Since World War II, the United States’ forward military presence has preserved a Free and Open Indo-Pacific contributing to generations of American prosperity. The President advocated for trilateral arms control negotiations between the United States, Russia, and China. The two leaders agreed to use the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” to describe the applicable emerging technologies. The two countries established the U.S.-China Super Intelligence (SI) Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to SI. The next exchange will occur by November 2026. The United States and China also agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for SI incidents.

title: First Lady Melania Trump Highlights Art, Culture, and the Next Generation During State Visit of President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan
text: Office of the First Lady First Lady Melania Trump Highlights Art, Culture, and the Next Generation During State Visit of President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan The White House September 25, 2026 “Art and culture have a remarkable ability to transcend borders, connect generations, and offer us a deeper appreciation for one another. It was an honor to welcome President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan and share with them the history, artistry, and traditions that help make America exceptional and our trans-Pacific relations so important,” said First Lady Melania Trump. President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump welcomed His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan to Washington, DC, for a historic State Visit this week, which included a State Arrival Ceremony on the South Lawn on Wednesday, September 24, 2026. The State Arrival Ceremony featured the United States Armed Forces, including a military review, performances by the United States Army Old Guard Fife and Drum Corps, the United States Marine Corps Silent Drill Platoon, and “The Commandant’s Own” United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps, and concluded with a military flyover featuring a B-2 Spirit and four F-22 Raptors. Following the Ceremony, the First Lady hosted Madame Peng for a special cultural program at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Asian Art, where they explored works representing centuries of artistic achievement and cultural exchange. Their visit included a viewing of a notched jade disk dating to China’s Shang dynasty, followed by the Smithsonian’s celebrated Peacock Room, created by American artist James McNeill Whistler. The First Lady and Madame Peng also viewed an 18th-century Qianlong-period Chinese porcelain vase, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship and decorative sophistication of imperial Chinese porcelain. The program concluded with the youth choir from Hope Chinese School performing “Jasmine Flower” and “Songs & Smiles” for the First Lady and Madame Peng. The children’s voices offered a fitting close to the visit, celebrating the beauty of artistic expression and the promise of the next generation. The First Lady led preparations for the State Dinner in the East Room of the White House later that evening, bringing together American culinary traditions and subtle Chinese influences. On Friday morning, the President and First Lady welcomed President Xi and Madame Peng to the White House for tea in the Red Room, continuing the traditions of hospitality that have long accompanied visits by foreign leaders and their spouses. Following tea, the President and First Lady accompanied President Xi and Madame Peng to the National Archives, where they viewed important records and documents highlighting America’s 250th birthday as well as important chapters in the history of the relationship between the United States and China. The visit offered an opportunity to reflect upon the history shared between two nations while looking toward the future. The State Visit concluded at the National Archives, where the President and First Lady bid farewell to President Xi and Madame Peng.
