title: First Lady Melania Trump Releases Details on the State Dinner with His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of The People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan
text: Office of the First Lady First Lady Melania Trump Releases Details on the State Dinner with His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of The People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan The White House September 24, 2026 President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump will welcome His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of The People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan for a State Dinner in the East Room of the White House this evening. The First Lady led the preparations for the dinner, which will be attended by the official delegations as well as business leaders and government officials. MENU The menu showcases American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence, bringing the culinary traditions of both nations together. The meal begins with a toast of Schramsberg “Blanc De Noir,” honoring the historic “Toast to Peace” shared by President Nixon and Premier Zhou Enlai in Beijing in 1972. The same American sparkling wine served at that historic gathering continues to be enjoyed at White House functions today. First Course Yellow Squash Velouté Wild Mushroom FricasséeCrispy Pancetta Scallion Oil The first course offers a refined and silky-smooth velouté made of sweet yellow squash. This course is gently blended to highlight its delicate seasonal flavors of earthy wild mushrooms, sautéed with fresh herbs. Together, these ingredients create a rich fricassee, complemented by crispy pancetta for a savory and smoky contrast. A finishing drizzle of scallion oil adds vibrance and a subtle allium brightness to the dish. Second Course Sesame Crusted Sea Bass Braised Baby Bok ChoyRoasted Garden Eggplant Sauce Verte The second course is prepared delicately with fresh seabass and coated in toasted sesame seeds. This combination creates a fragrant nutty crust while keeping the fish tender. The fish is served with crisp baby bok choy and roasted garden eggplant, creating lightly caramelized flavors. The dish is finished with a vibrant sauce verte of fresh herbs, which add brightness, acidity, and a garden character. Dessert Vanilla Crémeux & White House Honey Ice Cream Walnut FrangipaneSour Cherry Confit The dessert course is a smooth vanilla crémeux with a vibrant sour cherry confit center, set a top a rich walnut frangipane. The dessert’s fruit shaped form is complimented by a delicate ice cream made with harvested White House honey. ENTERTAINMENT There will be several performances during the formal dinner, which will be headlined by Mr. Christopher Macchio, a classically trained tenor who performed at the 2025 Presidential Inauguration. The evening’s entertainment will feature performances by military musicians from the United States Marines Corps and the United States Army, including “The President’s Own” United States Marine Band, “The Commandant’s Own” United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps, the United States Army Chorus, and the United States Army Strings. FLORAL & DÉCOR The décor for the evening is an expression of warmth and celebration and draws on the color red’s longstanding cultural significance throughout Chinese history. Urns showcase overflowing red blossoms. Tables are dressed in rich red linens and adorned with dahlias and ranunculus. Among the seasonal blooms, the tables feature vermeil from the White House collection. The Reagan State Service is featured on the tables. These details blend Chinese artistry and American tradition together, showcased within the timeless elegance of the White House.

title: First Lady Melania Trump and Madame Peng Liyuan Visit Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art Highlighting Sino-American Artwork, Culture, and the Next Generation
text: Office of the First Lady First Lady Melania Trump and Madame Peng Liyuan Visit Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art Highlighting Sino-American Artwork, Culture, and the Next Generation The White House September 24, 2026 First Lady Melania Trump and Madame Peng Liyuan visited the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, DC today, where they explored works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and cultural exchange and shared a special moment with students from the Washington, DC area. Upon arrival, the First Lady and Madame Peng were welcomed by leadership of the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art before beginning their tour of the museum’s collections. The First Lady and Madame Peng then viewed the Smithsonian’s celebrated Peacock Room , one of the museum’s most distinctive and immersive works of art. Created by American artist James McNeill Whistler in 1876–77, the Peacock Room transforms an entire interior into a dazzling composition of blue, green, and gold. Inspired in significant part by Chinese porcelain and Japanese design, Whistler covered the room with shimmering patterns and fanciful depictions of peacocks, creating a singular work in which painting, architecture, and decorative arts converge. Purchased by American collector Charles Lang Freer in 1904, the room was transported from London to the United States and has been a centerpiece of the museum in Washington since 1923. Today, the Peacock Room stands as a remarkable meeting point of American art and Asian artistic traditions, reflecting the ways artists and collectors have found inspiration across cultures and generations. The First Lady and Madame Peng continued their visit with a viewing of a Qianlong-period Chinese porcelain vase , dating to the 18th century. Produced in Jingdezhen during the Qing dynasty, the vase features elaborate floral decoration executed in colorful famille rose enamels, gold, and iron red over a pale glaze. The work is part of the Freer Gallery of Art’s collection and reflects the extraordinary technical and decorative sophistication of imperial Chinese porcelain during the Qianlong era. Museum leadership who served as guides for the visit were Jan Stuart, Melvin R. Seiden Curator of Chinese Art at the National Museum of Asian Art, and Chase Robinson, Dame Jillian Sackler Director of the Arthur M. Sackler Gallery and Freer Gallery of Art. The visit concluded with a musical performance by the youth choir from Hope Chinese School, who performed “Jasmine Flower” and “Songs & Smiles” for the First Lady and Madame Peng. The young students’ performance offered a joyful and memorable conclusion to the visit, bringing together the beauty of artistic expression, the appreciation of cultural heritage, and the shared experience of young people discovering the enduring power of art and music.

title: AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA AND THE GOVERNMENT OF THE KINGDOM OF DENMARK TOGETHER WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF GREENLAND
text: Briefings & Statements AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA AND THE GOVERNMENT OF THE KINGDOM OF DENMARK TOGETHER WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF GREENLAND The White House September 22, 2026 AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA AND THE GOVERNMENT OF THE KINGDOM OF DENMARK TOGETHER WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF GREENLAND TO AMEND AND SUPPLEMENT THE AGREEMENT OF 27 APRIL 1951 PURSUANT TO THE NORTH ATLANTIC TREATY BETWEEN THE GOVERNMENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA AND THE GOVERNMENT OF THE KINGDOM OF DENMARK ON THE DEFENSE OF GREENLAND (1951 DEFENSE AGREEMENT), INCLUDING ALL RELEVANT SUBSEQUENT AGREEMENTS RELATED THERETO Preamble The Government of the United States of America (hereinafter “the United States”) and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark (hereinafter “the Kingdom of Denmark”) together with the Government of Greenland (hereinafter “Greenland”), hereinafter referred to collectively as “the Parties” and singularly as a “Party”; Cognizant of the rights and obligations deriving from the 1949 North Atlantic Treaty, and considering that Greenland through the Kingdom of Denmark has been a part of NATO since then; Recalling the long history of cooperation between the Parties based on their deep respect for democracy, human rights, and the rule of law, as well as the more than eighty years of close defense cooperation between them, which has contributed to strengthening the security and stability of the United States, Greenland, and the rest of the North Atlantic Treaty area; Reaffirming the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, and recognizing that the People of Greenland constitute a people pursuant to international law with the right to self-determination; Noting that the procedure for Greenlandic independence is set out in Article 21 of Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009 on Greenland Self-Government; Recognizing the Parties’ respective obligations and commitments under international law as well as national legal frameworks, including all existing agreements between the Parties; Recognizing the need to protect the pristine environment of Greenland and reaffirming Article VI concerning Protection of the Environment in the 1991 Memorandum of Understanding, as well as the 2004 Joint Declaration; Recognizing the economic, social, and cultural rights of the People of Greenland, including with respect to their lands and their way of life, including hunting, fishing, and other traditional, cultural, historical, future activities, and developments; Considering that the Defense Arrangements have promoted stability and well-being in the North Atlantic Treaty area by uniting the Parties’ efforts for collective defense and preserved peace and security as well as developed their collective capacity to resist armed attack; Recognizing the United States’ indispensable historical and ongoing contributions to the security and defense of Greenland and the rest of the North Atlantic Treaty area, including significant sacrifices and billions of dollars spent over the better part of a century, dating back to before World War II and the establishment of NATO, and the irreplaceable role the United States military plays in the defense of the territory of Greenland now and in the future; Acknowledging the reopening of the U.S. Consulate in Nuuk and the U.S. contributions to mutual scientific and educational cooperation and exchanges, minerals cooperation, cooperation on economic development and business promotion, and cultural and local partnerships together with Greenland; Acknowledging as well Greenland’s contribution to the Parties’ mutual security interests and its consequent sharing of the associated risks and responsibilities, and the commitment of the Parties to continuing close cooperation within NATO in ensuring North Atlantic security, as set forth in the 2004 Igaliku Agreement; Recognizing the security challenges in the Arctic and the High North posed by adversaries’ increased military activity and growing strategic interest in the region; Recognizing the Parties’ common goal of international peace and peaceful co-existence, and respecting the important contribution of Greenland to this goal; Reaffirming the common goal of maximizing real, tangible, and substantial benefits to the People of Greenland from the Defense Areas; Noting that the security situation in the Arctic is changing and that more efforts are needed to ensure security there in the future; Recognizing the Parties’ shared interest in allowing the United States to have military access to the territory of Greenland to the extent necessary to defend the North Atlantic Treaty area, Greenland, and the American continent, including through establishment of a Golden Dome defense system; and Wishing therefore to further amend and supplement the Defense Arrangements, so as to strengthen them and reinforce their permanent nature, Hereby agree as follows: I. Objectives This Agreement amending and supplementing the Defense Arrangements shall facilitate the ability of the Parties to take any measures necessary or appropriate to carry out expeditiously their respective and joint responsibilities in Greenland, including to defend the North Atlantic Treaty area, Greenland, and the American continent, while respecting the interests of and providing benefits for the Greenlandic society. II. NATO engagement The Parties support a stronger NATO engagement in the Arctic, including as regards planning, presence, exercises, and joint intelligence gathering. III. Definitions For the purposes of this Agreement: “1949 North Atlantic Treaty” means the North Atlantic Treaty signed at Washington on April 4, 1949. “1951 Defense Agreement” means the Agreement Pursuant to the North Atlantic Treaty between the United States and the Kingdom of Denmark Concerning the Defense of Greenland, signed at Copenhagen on April 27, 1951. “1991 Memorandum of Understanding” means the Memorandum of Understanding between the United States and the Kingdom of Denmark, including the Home Rule Government of Greenland, Concerning the Use of Sondrestrom Aviation Facility, Kulusuk Airfield and Other Matters Related to United States Military Activities in Greenland, done in Copenhagen, March 13, 1991. “2004 Igaliku Agreement” means the Agreement between the United States and the Kingdom of Denmark, including the Home Rule Government of Greenland, to Amend and Supplement the 1951 Defense Agreement, Including Relevant Subsequent Agreements Related Thereto, signed at Igaliku on August 6, 2004. “2004 Joint Declaration” means the Joint Declaration on Cooperation on the Environment in Greenland between the Parties issued on August 6, 2004 in Igaliku. “2020 Diplomatic Notes” means the exchange of diplomatic notes between the United States and the Kingdom of Denmark concerning contracting, dated October 27, 2020. “Defense Area” means an area in Greenland where the United States establishes and/or operates a military base consistent with the Defense Arrangements. “Defense Arrangements” means the 1951 Defense Agreement, together with subsequent amending and supplementing agreements and related non-binding arrangements between the Parties, as set out in Annex 1. “Greenland Self-Government Law” means the Act no. 473 of 12 June 2009 on Greenland Self-Government. “Permanent Committee” means a committee established under the 1991 Memorandum of Understanding to facilitate consultation and exchange of information on matters relating to the United States military presence in Greenland. “Particularly Sensitive Sectors or Activities” means sectors or activities determined to be particularly sensitive, including but not limited to critical infrastructure and the extraction of resources. “Territorial Waters” means the territorial sea around Greenland as laid down in national law by the Kingdom of Denmark in accordance with the international law of the sea as reflected in the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. IV. Defense Areas The Parties shall make best use of the procedures set out in the Defense Arrangements, including the 1951 Defense Agreement and the 2004 Igaliku Agreement, as amended and supplemented herein, to enable the following: i. The United States shall be allowed to modernize and expand its activities in Pituffik Space Base; ii. The United States shall be allowed to establish an additional Defense Area at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig in accordance with modalities and technical details to be mutually agreed by the Parties; iii. The United States may establish additional defense areas in Greenland and strengthen its military operations or facilities. Either Party may identify the need for a new Defense Area for the defense of the North Atlantic Treaty area, Greenland, and the American continent. Such Party shall provide a proposal describing the location, scope, size, and types of activities of the proposed Defense Area as well as other modalities such as mitigating measures, including those necessary to take account of the 1991 Memorandum of Understanding and the 2004 Joint Declaration. The Parties shall immediately convene to engage in consultations through the Permanent Committee to decide implementation details based on mutual agreement. If no agreement is reached within 90 days at the Permanent Committee, consultations shall escalate to the deputy minister level, followed by the minister level; iv. The United States shall award all contracts to commercial enterprises for goods and services related to the establishment, maintenance and servicing, including, but not limited to, construction and dismantling projects, of Defense Areas in Greenland to Greenlandic sources to the maximum extent possible, taking into account the capabilities and feasibility of such sources to implement contracts. To secure contracts to Greenlandic sources, the Parties agree to update the 2020 Diplomatic Notes accordingly. V. Unmanned military installations The Kingdom of Denmark together with Greenland shall review requests to establish unmanned military installations in Greenland outside of the Defense Areas under accelerated governmental approval procedures. The request shall include a proposal describing the location, scope, size, and types of activities of the proposed unmanned military installation, as well as other modalities such as mitigating measures, including those necessary to take account of the 1991 Memorandum of Understanding and the 2004 Joint Declaration. Article IV(iv.) of this Agreement shall apply to the establishment, maintenance, and servicing of such unmanned military installations. VI. United States military access, basing and overflight As regards United States access to the rest of the territory of Greenland (including the Territorial Waters), the following shall apply: With a view to ensuring a secure and effective operation of the Defense Areas, the United States of America shall enjoy, for its public vessels and aircraft and its armed forces and vehicles, the right of free access to and movement between the Defense Areas through Greenland, including the Territorial Waters, by land, air and sea. This may also apply to unmanned military installations subject to agreement bythe Parties on the modalities at the time of establishment; United States aircraft may fly over and land in any territory in Greenland, including the Territorial Waters, and United States public vessels may have undersea access to and movement within the Territorial Waters, without restriction except as mutually agreed upon by the Parties; United States public vessels shall be given such additional access to and movement within the Territorial Waters as isagreed to by the Parties at any given time to be required by the military situation for the defense of the North Atlantic Treaty area, Greenland, and the American continent, or for other purposes as may be agreed bythe Parties. These rights must be exercised in a manner that respects the Greenlandic society and the Greenlandic way of life, including hunting, fishing, and other traditional, cultural, historical, and other future activities, to the maximum extent possible. The implementation of this Article will be addressed regularly at the Permanent Committee. VII. Security of the Defense Areas and prevention of espionage The Parties agree that the territory in the vicinity of a Defense Area shall not be used in any manner that threatens the security of the Defense Area. In order to implement this requirement, the Parties intend to cooperate with respect to ensuring the security of the Defense Areas. The United States shall have the right to raise concerns regarding construction, or change of use in a manner that threatens a Defense Area, of any building, facility, or installation in the vicinity of the Defense Area. Upon such notification the Parties shall mutually determine what steps may be necessary to address any threat. The Parties shall work together to counter espionage in Greenland. Relevant authorities in the Kingdom of Denmark shall keep in close contact with relevant U.S. authorities and other partners to the fullest extent necessary to implement this Article. VIII. Defense posture by the Kingdom of Denmark The Kingdom of Denmark has strengthened and shall continue to strengthen its security posture in the Arctic through comprehensive, multi-domain approach encompassing land, maritime, air and space capabilities. Through enhanced presence, improved surveillance and increased cooperation and interoperability with NATO-Allies, the Kingdom of Denmark shall continue to address emerging threats and contribute to collective stability and security in the Arctic region. IX. Establishment of manned or unmanned military installations by third states No state that is not a member of NATO shall be allowed to establish its own manned or unmanned military installations in Greenland nor shall they be allowed a persistent presence of military forces in Greenland, unless otherwise agreed by the Parties. X. Foreign direct investment and other activities Given the threat to national security and public order posed by increased efforts by adversaries to expand influence and control in Greenland, the Parties agree that states or investors from a state that is not a member of NATO, a NATO partner, or an EU member state shall not be allowed to have (i) control, (ii) significant influence, or (iii) access to non-public information that may constitute a threat to national security or public order within Particularly Sensitive Sectors or Activities in the territory of Greenland (including the Territorial Waters), unless agreed between the Parties that the activities of such states or investors would not constitute a threat to national security or public order. The objective shall be ensured by Greenland in close cooperation with the authorities of the Kingdom of Denmark in its application of any of its current or future investment screening laws. Relevant authorities in the Kingdom of Denmark shall engage in close consultation with relevant United States authorities and other partners. The specific modalities for that close consultation shall be determined by the relevant authorities. XI. Permanent nature of this Agreement This Agreement does not have an end date and may only be amended by mutual consent in accordance with Article XIII of the 1951 Defense Agreement. In case Greenland exercises its right to self-determination to become independent, the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark and the Government of Greenland shall together ensure that the independent Greenlandic state will (i) agree to remain in NATO, including by applying to become a member if necessary, and (ii) affirmatively assume, as from the date of independence, all of the rights and obligations of the Kingdom of Denmark specified in this Agreement, including any implementation agreements or arrangements between the Parties, as well as the Defense Arrangements. XII. Entry into force This Agreement shall enter into force on the date of a diplomatic note informing the United States of the completion of necessary parliamentary procedures by the Kingdom of Denmark together with Greenland. Done at New York on the 22nd day of September, 2026, in triplicate in the English, Danish, and Greenlandic languages. In the event of ambiguity or conflict between the versions, the English language version shall prevail. Annex 1 Key agreements in the Defense Arrangements include, inter alia : Main agreement: Agreement of 27 April 1951 between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark, pursuant to the North Atlantic Treaty, concerning the defense of Greenland Additional agreements and related non-binding arrangements: Exchange of Notes of 31 May 1968 between the Government of the United States of America and the Kingdom of Denmark supplementing the Agreement of 27 April 1951. Memorandum of Understanding of 13 March 1991 between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark (Including the Home Rule Government of Greenland) concerning the use of Sondrestrom Aviation Facility, Kulusuk Airfield and Other Matters Related to the United States Military Activities in Greenland Memorandum of Understanding of 20 February 2003 between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark (Including Greenland Home Rule Government) Concerning the Dundas Area Agreement of 6 August 2004 between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark, Including the Home Rule Government of Greenland, to Amend and Supplement the Agreement of 27 April 1951, Including Relevant Subsequent Agreements Related Thereto Joint Declaration of 6 August 2004 by the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark, Including the Home Rule Government of Greenland, on Economic and Technical Cooperation Joint Declaration of 6 August 2004 by the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark, Including the Home Rule Government of Greenland, on Cooperation on the Environment in Greenland Joint Statement of 28 October 2020 on Improved Cooperation in Greenland; Exchange of Notes of 27 October 2020; and Common Plan for U.S.-Greenland Cooperation in Support of our Understanding for Pituffik (Thule Air Base) signed 28 October 2020 Relevant NATO agreements: North Atlantic Treaty of 4 April 1949 Agreement of 19 June 1951 between the Parties to the North Atlantic Treaty regarding the status of their forces (“NATO-SOFA”)

title: First Lady Melania Trump Unveils New Fostering the Future Together Technology Alliances, International Events, and Membership Expansion
text: Office of the First lady First Lady Melania Trump Unveils New Fostering the Future Together Technology Alliances, International Events, and Membership Expansion The White House September 22, 2026 First Lady Melania Trump today reconvened members of Fostering the Future Together during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. The First Lady welcomed leaders from around the world, including representatives from the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Republic of Korea, the Philippines, Poland, Ukraine, Türkiye, the United Arab Emirates, Panama, Canada, and other nations. First Lady Melania Trump remarked, “Together, we are a beautiful range of cultures, languages, histories, and traditions. And yet, we stand unified around one everlasting truth: the future of our world will be determined by what we do for our children today.” First Lady Melania Trump unveiled several upcoming Fostering the Future Together events for 2026: G20, hosted by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump ASEAN Conference, hosted by First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos of the Philippines European Regional Meeting, hosted by First Lady Marta Nawrocka of Poland Caribbean Regional Meeting, hosted by First Lady Diani Prince-Drew of Saint Kitts and Nevis “When nations speak with one voice, the world listens. Our collective influence is profound. Together, we can open doors, move markets, shape policy. And most importantly, we can change lives for the better,” First Lady Melania Trump said. First Lady Melania Trump also announced new private-sector technology partnerships with Adobe, Amazon, Intel, Starlink, Google, and Zoom. Tim Cook, Executive Chairman of Apple and Enrique Lores, CEO of PayPal, also attended. The First Lady welcomed new member nations, expanding Fostering the Future Together to fifty-seven participating countries. Calling on the assembled First Spouses to act, First Lady Melania Trump said, “Our Fostering the Future Together coalition must strive to empower the youth of our nations to: bend the boundaries of imagination, explore new frontiers of intellect, have the courage to take calculated risks, and build toward advancement of society.” About Fostering the Future Together: Fostering the Future Together is a global coalition of nations unified to empower children through technology and education. First Lady Melania Trump announced Fostering the Future Together during the 80th United Nations General Assembly. In spring 2026, she convened the initiative’s two-day Global Coalition Summit in Washington DC, bringing together First Spouses and technology-sector leaders at the United States Department of State. The gathering culminated at the White House, where the First Lady welcomed the largest assembly of First Spouses ever convened there for diplomatic purposes in U.S. history. The First Lady’s remarks, as prepared for delivery, are below. Fostering the Future Together Expands Nation Memberships, Private-Sector Commitments, & Unveils New Events Thank you, Special Envoy Wallace and Ambassador Waltz. Your ongoing commitment to support Fostering the Future Together is both important and meaningful. Friends, Excellencies, and Distinguished Leaders. Welcome to New York City. Fostering the Future Together now unites nearly 60 nations, many represented here today. You have traveled great distances in support of our children, bringing together distinguished leaders from Panama, the Republic of Korea, Kenya, Albania, Estonia, Dominican Republic, Guatemala and beyond. Together, we are a beautiful range of cultures, languages, histories, and traditions. And yet, we stand unified around one everlasting truth: the future of our world will be determined by what we do for our children today. Fostering the Future Together is more than a coalition. It is a commitment to empower children through technology and education, to ensure that every child, regardless of where they are born, has the opportunity to imagine, learn, create, and thrive. When nations speak with one voice, the world listens. Our collective influence is profound. Together, we can open doors, move markets, shape policy. And most importantly, we can change lives for the better. Each of us has been entrusted with the responsibility of leadership. But mark my words, our success will not be measured solely by what we accomplish during our time in this role. Our success as leaders will be measured by what remains after we are gone. Did we strengthen our schools? Did we make new discoveries possible? Did we inspire greater innovation? And most importantly, will the next generation be able to build upon our vision and use our accomplishments to advance their careers, families, communities, and nations? So, I ask you: Will you join me and lead? Will you put the future of our children above the differences that divide us? Fostering the Future Together is a global coalition with a unified mission: to empower children through technology and education. But what does it mean to empower a child? True empowerment begins by giving a child the confidence to believe that their mind has value. It means giving children the freedom to imagine a world beyond the one they know today and the confidence, knowledge, and tools to make the vision real. Our Fostering the Future Together coalition must strive to empower the youth of our nations to: Bend the boundaries of imagination, Explore new frontiers of intellect, Have the courage to take calculated risks, and Build toward advancement of society. When we succeed, we will create a stronger world shaped by a new generation of people capable of building healthier communities, with greater tolerance for one another, advanced technologies, food security, new industries, and widespread prosperity. The people in this room today can prepare our children and our grandchildren not simply to inherit the world—but to improve it. That is empowerment. We are living in an extraordinary moment in human history. We stand together at the threshold of a technological revolution. Ideas once confined to science-fiction novels and films have become part of our everyday reality. What once seemed impossible is becoming ordinary. Today, we can converse with AI, video call our families from any place on the planet, hold an entire computer in the palm of our hand, use self-driving cars, enter virtual worlds, and use biometric ID to access our bank accounts, airport terminals, and homes. The list is exhaustive. Artificial intelligence is transforming entire business sectors and expanding how humanity accesses the largest corpus of information ever available to humanity. But access alone is not empowerment. We must give our children the tools—and teach them how to use those tools wisely. I would also like to take a minute to thank our private-sector tech companies who have also stepped up to empower our children: Adobe, Amazon, Google, Starlink, Zoom, and Intel. Thank you for empowering children with access to technology, all over the planet. When we gathered at the White House for the inaugural meeting of Fostering the Future Together, we witnessed something very powerful. Our first spouses were inspired to act—and several made meaningful commitments. I thank Ms. Marcos from the Philippines, who has committed to hosting a Fostering the Future Together event at the upcoming ASEAN conference in Manila. Poland’s Marta Nawrocka will host a regional European Fostering the Future Together event for members this winter. The First Lady of Saint Kitts and Nevis, Diani Prince-Drew, is organizing and hosting our Caribbean Fostering the Future Together conference before the new year–perfect timing to gather in that beautiful region of the world. Thank you. And in December, I will host Fostering the Future Together’s first G20 event in Miami, Florida. To the leaders of these great nations: thank you for stepping forward to activate your regions. You will have my full support. Years from now, our children may not remember the meetings we held or the speeches we gave. But they will live with the consequences of what we do here. So, let history say that at a moment of extraordinary possibility, leaders from around the world came together through Fostering the Future Together and chose to put children first.

title: First Lady Melania Trump Releases Details Ahead of His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of The People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan’s Visit to The White House
text: Office of the First Lady First Lady Melania Trump Releases Details Ahead of His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of The People’s Republic of China, and Madame Peng Liyuan’s Visit to The White House The White House September 21, 2026 President Donald J. Trump and First Lady Melania Trump will welcome His Excellency Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China and Madame Peng Liyuan to the White House on Thursday, September 24, 2026, for an official state visit. This visit comes more than a decade since President Xi and Madame Peng’s last visit to the White House, marking a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries. On Wednesday, September 23, the President will greet His Excellency, Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China and Madame Peng Liyuan at Joint Base Andrews. On Thursday morning, September 24, the President and First Lady will host a State Arrival Ceremony honoring His Excellency, Xi Jinping, President of the People’s Republic of China and Madame Peng Liyuan. The ceremony, which will be held on the South Lawn, State Floor, and Rose Garden of the White House, will feature 479 military personnel, representing all branches of the United States Armed Forces. As the arrival begins, the South Drive will be lined with the Armed Forces Full Honor Cordon leading to a national flag display of U.S. and China flags where the United States Army Herald Trumpets will present a fanfare on the South Portico as the President and First Lady welcome His Excellency Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan to the White House. On the State Floor, “The President’s Own” United States Marine Band will play the national anthems of the People’s Republic of China and the United States of America, followed by remarks from both The President and His Excellency Xi Jinping. The ceremony will also feature a Presidential Salute from the United States Marine Silent Drill Platoon and United States Joint Forces Command on the South Lawn. There will then be a Military Review in the Rose Garden where The United States Army Herald Trumpets will line the roof of the West and Oval Colonnades. Military demonstrations will be performed by the United States Army Old Guard Fife and Drum Corps, the United States Marine Corps Silent Drill Platoon, and “The Commandant’s Own” United States Marine Drum and Bugle Corps. The ceremony will conclude with a military flyover featuring a B-2 Spirit and four F-22 Raptors. After the arrival ceremony, Mrs. Trump and Madame Peng Liyuan will visit the Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art to explore works spanning centuries of artistic achievement and Sino-American cultural exchange. On Thursday evening, the President and First Lady will greet His Excellency Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan upon their arrival to the North Portico of the White House for a State Dinner in the East Room. The Office of the First Lady will share additional details on the State Dinner on Wednesday, September 23. On Friday morning, the President and First Lady will greet His Excellency Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan upon their arrival to the South Portico of the White House for tea in the Red Room of the White House. Afterward, the couples will travel to the National Archives in Washington, DC where they will view a variety of important records and documents significant to the American and Chinese relationship throughout history. To conclude the historic State visit, the President and First Lady will bid farewell to His Excellency and Madame Peng Liyuan at the National Archives.

title: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth SpSecretary of War Pete Hegseth Speech on the Arsenal of Freedom in Austin, TX (As Delivered)
text: SECRETARY OF WAR PETE HEGSETH: Thank you, Dino. Thank you for that incredible introduction. I remember that speech. In fact, it was about a year ago, and we pledged to wage a war of attrition against the Pentagon bureaucracy to open our building up to companies just like this one, to fast runners that are ready to run hard, build at scale, take risks, invest, are doing it for the right reasons. We can't just have the big companies at the top doing all the work and not doing it fast enough. We need the best companies in this country, American manufacturing, American made, and that's what you're doing right here at Saronic, right here in Texas for the Arsenal of Freedom tour. It's great to be here with you. Just since we are here in Texas, I want to thank a couple of, they become dear friends and great advocates for your company or your state, but also for what we're doing in our department. Congressman August Pfluger and Morgan Luttrell. I see Morgan right there. Congressman Pfluger and Congressman Luttrell have been not just with me from day one, but with our cause from day one. Backing us up when things were difficult, when things were easy, when they were good, when they were bad, when we were having to tell hard truths. They've had our back. So, gentlemen, thank you very much for everything you do for us. Appreciate it. So we've traveled the country, meeting with great companies and innovators. And one thing is for certain: thanks to President Trump, thanks to the efforts of the Department of War, but more importantly to great Americans like you, American manufacturing is back. American-made is back, and not a minute too soon. And not for show, not for peacetime, but for victory, a lasting victory, one that will secure our freedoms for generations to come. Now, having had a chance to tour this facility firsthand just a few moments ago, the scale, investment, and precision of your projects is truly impressive. You are on the front lines of American industry. And that's the entire purpose of the Arsenal of Freedom tour. I had a chance to shake some hands along the assembly line there, the production line, but the point, as Dino said, of this tour is to look patriots in the eye and thank you for the work that you've done and for the work that you're doing. Every helmet out there slinging lead on our behalf is doing it because of a hard hat enabling them that stands behind them. That's you. That's your mission inside this company with what you're building with these beautiful boats, ships, whatever the navy calls them…vessels, thank you very much, on behalf of our warfighters. But I know, and you especially know more than I do, that the greatness of Saronic was not simply wished into existence. It didn't appear in thin air. What exists between these walls was forged. It was forged by the investment and the labor and the expertise and the sheer willpower of each of you standing here today. In some ways, I would say this a call this a field of dreams company. Remember the phrase: If you build it, they will come. In some ways, that's what Saronic has done. You built it knowing we need it, and we are here because we're going to use it, and we appreciate everything you put into it. You know this here in Texas, but the political swamp creatures in Washington D.C. They see they just don't necessarily understand that mission. They're experts in the art of sitting back, lobbying, collecting a government paycheck, and coasting off the labor of what was built by others. They produce nothing, build nothing, or worse, they outsource it and then block out competitors in our own country. But you are the innovators, the builders of the Arsenal of Freedom. It is precisely the strength of our domestic manufacturing and arsenal and industry that keeps us free. American manufacturing, American made, American jobs, American power. And as Morgan reminded me, nobody does it bigger than Texas. It's a fact. The future of warfare will be built on the backs of AI and autonomy, which is a top priority of this War Department to ensure our warfighters, whether they see less direct conflict or not, and they probably will see less direct conflict because of autonomy, but they'll be more lethal, which is what's even more important. Saronic is the gold standard of what a company should be doing to achieve this. Take, for example, in the past, recovery missions required manned ships to conduct search and rescue in the direct line of adversary fire, like say the Strait of Hormuz. Well, just this last June, 2 U.S. Army AH-64 Apache pilots went down in contested waters near Oman. Saronic’s rapidly fielded, and I can attest it was rapidly fielded. Twenty four-foot autonomous vessel built right here in Austin, the Corsair USV, navigated forward and safely pulled the two pilots out of harm's way, marking the first known combat search and rescue mission executed by an autonomous vessel in American history. You did that. Those pilots are alive today because of the incredible innovation under this very roof. You should be, and rightfully are, incredibly proud of that feat. I just would…I remember that day thinking, "What the faces of those pilots must have looked like? What is this thing? Where are the sailors? Do I trust it? Does it speak to me? I remember thinking the options were the Omani Coast Guard. There were other things, and then an hour later, the report came to me…no, no, no, it was the unmanned surface vessel. I just thought only America. Only our companies, only our innovators, only our workers, and you raced it to the battlefield, and it has had great effect. The Corsair is also proving itself on offense in combat strike operations. In July, CENTCOM, you've seen the video. I've seen it. The world's seen it. Employed the Corsair to strike a submarine and ship maintenance facility at the Bandar Abbas Naval Base in the Persian Gulf. The operation degraded Iran's ability to continue attacking commercial shipping and marked the first operational employment of sea drones in U.S. military combat operations. Now, those are the kind of firsts that we like. What Saronic demonstrates is the future of American naval power, delivering over 300 combat-proven Corsairs, rapidly fielding the 52-foot Mirage, and scaling blue water reach with the 180-foot Marauder, all built in under a year. In our building, we're used to timelines of seven, eight years, one year is not a thing. It's like you're a mirage. But I came to see that it's real. That's the kind of scale and speed that our department needs, the kind of competition our building needs, the bureaucracy needs to realize that it can be done. Because if we go at the pace we've done in the past, we won't have what the warfighters of today and the future actually need. You are no longer testing concepts; you are deploying lethal autonomous mass to ensure our fleet commands the sea. You are the front lines of American power. You see, part of what makes Saronic exceptional is not just the technology; it's the warfighter DNA driven into every line of code and every weld, founded and operated by Veterans like the man who introduced me, Navy SEAL veteran Dino Mavrookas, eight combat tours. Marine veteran Rob Lehman. This team builds with the urgency of those who know firsthand what is at stake. And then partnering directly with our SkillBridge program and our service academies, Serana creates a premier pipeline for military and Veteran talent. Just as critically, you are transitioning skilled civilian American welders and machinists and fabricators from automotive and aerospace industries into cutting-edge naval shipbuilding. All I can say to that is more, please. We, thousands of miles away, are deeply and profoundly grateful for the work that you do, day in and day out. And I'm here on behalf of a president who demands the urgency, innovation, and combat power that this place delivers every single day. A president who has, from his very first day in office, operated on core principles of pure and unadulterated common sense. We put America, American citizens, and America first. The only real path to American security and strength is peace through strength. And a nation that cannot build for itself, a nation that cannot create its own tools, its own defenses, or its own future, is a nation that is in managed decline. And for too long, elites, especially on one side, but in both parties, sat idly by and accepted a backward status quo, but not President Trump. He recognized that decline is indeed a choice, a choice that must be fundamentally rejected in real time. And in doing so, he has unleashed a great American revival, a reawakening of the American industrial spirit and national confidence, as he calls it, rightfully so, a golden age for America that you are all a part of in this building. As his Secretary of War, my mission is to ignite this revival within our armed forces. And since day one, that mission has had three pillars upon which we stand. First, we're reviving the warrior ethos within our fighting force, reminding our warriors that their sole purpose is to be the most lethal fighting force on the planet. Full stop. We're not here to do social engineering, or social justice, or gender bending, or DEI, or dudes and dresses. We're just back to basics. That's what we do at the War Department. Second, we're rebuilding our military. We've seen a historic trillion-dollar investment thus far in the last budget, and you will see even more. And not just in platforms but in people. We're asking for $1.5 trillion in the current budget to make generational investments to keep our country strong and sustain good, high-paying jobs for American manufacturers like Saronic. We will deliver on this generational investment, we will fund this department. The president is committed to it, as are we, as are our partners in Congress, as are these congressmen and their colleagues in the Senate. We will deliver this generational funding and investment, come hell or high water. It just got me thinking. Speaking of hell or high water, those are two things the Iranian Navy are very familiar with at this point. Third, we are reestablishing deterrence. Under the previous administration, the world questioned American strength, and that is no more. The era of doubt and decline is over. Deterrence is back, and the world has taken notice. See, the department we're prudent, but we don't make weapons to store them in piggy banks. We use them to achieve American objectives. Hard power. When narco-terrorists, the Al Qaeda of our hemisphere, when they send drugs to our shores to poison Americans, we no longer catch and release those narco-terrorists. We sink their boats. Deterrence in action. When our southern border was overwhelmed by an illegal invasion, we secured it. Zero crossings, absolute sovereignty, deterrence in action. When American justice was required in Venezuela, hundreds of our best went downtown Caracas, grabbed a dictator, and returned without a single U.S. casualty. Deterrence in action. And when President Trump says that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, he means it. Iran has tried and is trying to blackmail the world with conventional weapons. It's the North Korea approach. So many conventional weapons that they can at their choosing race for a nuclear bomb. Well, under this president, that will never work. The devastation of our military against Iran has been historic. Even if the sheer lies of our so-called media act in service of Iranian state TV. You see, the only media that does fake propaganda better than Iran is our Trump deranged media. I'm serious. It's sad because we've got warriors in harm's way doing incredible things-a difficult, dangerous mission-and we have a deranged media that hate our president more than they love our country. We'll do our job no matter what. We will complete the mission. Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. President Trump holds the cards, deterrence in action. But to win the future as we will, we must build. The Department of War, as Dino mentioned, has been kicking the door wide open for commercial disruptors, non-traditional innovators, and venture-backed builders. We're actively creating the next generation of defense primes, firms like Saronic. Our Arsenal of Freedom tour showcases how modern deterrence requires commercial speed. Our chief technology officer, Emil Michael, who's with us here today, he helped unite our innovation ecosystem under one roof to expedite decisions instead of holding on to legacy bureaucratic delays. When I talk about a war of attrition against the Pentagon bureaucracy, Emil and I and our colleagues stand back to back, machine guns out every single day. And this brings me to my promise and my challenge to every industry leader in this country: the days of rewarding the comfortable old guard for stagnation and failure are over. We are a different department than we were two years ago, night and day. You see, I don't care what name is on the side of a vessel, or a missile, or a ship. I just want the best. And for too long, it was an oligarchy of a few companies that held everybody out. And our job is to rip that building open and allow the competition to be level, so that any great company in America can compete to build that vessel, that missile, or that ship. And the fastest runner will win. And if it's not Saronic, fine. But if it's Saronic, great. Whoever it is, whoever's the best, will win at today's War Department. We're moving from bureaucracy to business. The acquisitions reforms we've made, the emphasis on a modern technology stack, the way we're working with industry, all centered around the capabilities and speed needed for a modern military. We will provide larger, longer, and more predictable contracts to companies like Serrano, companies that can actually deliver at pace and at scale. We will reward leaders who choose to invest in their workers, who expand their capacity, who share in our sense of urgency. That's been one of the biggest things we've had to infuse into the defense industrial base: a sense of urgency. We reward those who choose to deploy their resources toward bolstering production, as you have in multiple facilities, instead of stock buyback programs. The message is simple: If you deliver for America, this Pentagon, this War Department, will have your back. If you do not, we will show you the door. And look at what Saronic is doing for Texas and for Louisiana. In Texas, under the governor's leadership, we are witnessing the rebirth of American maritime power. Since 2022, Saronic has scaled up to over 1,200 Texas employees, operating 540,000 square feet across Austin and conducting cutting-edge maritime trials in Galveston. Saronic's partnership with the department is projected to generate over 260 billion dollars in economic impact for the Lone Star State alone. At the port of Brownsville, Port Alpha, pretty impressive, I must say, delivers a $3 billion investment, up to 10,000 high-paying jobs, over 160 billion in regional impact for Cameron County, and 150,000…this is what I love to hear, gross tons of new shipbuilding capacity. The industrial muscle here will double domestic shipbuilding and ensure absolute dominance. This momentum. It'll also transform Louisiana, and the governor there is restoring working waterfronts. We need to revive and bring back our waterfronts. Through modernizing the historic Gulf craft shipyard in Franklin and establishing a new engineering hub in New Orleans, Saronic is executing a 300 million, 300 plus million investment to build autonomous surface vessels. This effort creates over 1,500 high-paying maritime careers. So together, Franklin and New Orleans prove that combining historic craft with robotics creates an unbeatable industrial edge. You see, in complex theaters like the Pacific, deterrence demands capability, capacity, but also, and most importantly, credibility-a credible capability, a credible threat. Innovation like what is happening at Saronic will allow us to deliver the kind of magazine depth, operational unpredictability, and create targeting dilemmas for adversaries. We are fielding, each and every day, that arsenal of freedom that will be required on that edge. Saronic embodies this sovereign standard on the shop floor. Again, from the edge to the shop floor. That's how I need you, I want you to think about it every single day. That's the essence of the arsenal of freedom. What you do is not just build a widget; you build a sword, a tool, a vessel for a warfighter halfway around the globe who utterly depends on your precision, on your lethality, on what you put in their hands. And the Corsair is manufactured in an important way entirely with American materials and hands sourced through a network of 94 American suppliers across 27-not 27 countries, 27 American states. American-made, American manufacturing, American jobs, American power. Because as you know, our American warriors-they are second to none, the best in the world and the best of our country, the real 1%. You know, in places like Washington D.C., New York City, Austin, they like to talk about the elite, the 1%, the privileged. No, no, no. The real 1% are the ones you serve, are the ones I serve, the men and women who raise the right hand to defend our republic, who put their life on the line in dark, dangerous, difficult places and sign up to defend us, to defend me and defend you. They are the absolute real 1%, the real elite of our nation. But while our warriors are that 1% and the tip of the spear, you are what sharpens them. All the strategies from the Pentagon are meaningless without the people on this floor, the technicians, the machinists, the fabricators, and the engineers. Every platform you weld, wire, and assemble gives our warfighters the decisive edge to win and return home. Never forget that direct line from your hands to the success of our warfighters. So today I say to you, build faster, scale larger, and deliver more. We need you like never before, because when America is unleashed, we win. But I hear that when Texas is unleashed, we dominate. It's incredible to work through a president who has reminded me time and time again to remind the war fighters time and time again that he has their back. It's all-it's the one thing I always wanted to hear when I was a lieutenant, a platoon leader leading men in combat. I needed to know that my commander had my back if I had to make a difficult decision. And so everywhere I go, talking to troops that will have a chance to do that today, and to the corps of cadets at A&M tomorrow, reminding them that we will have their back, that the president has their back that they are unleashed to fight with violence and decisiveness against our enemies, which is what which is what is required in a combat scenario. Just know that while we have their back, you have theirs, and I think there's been no better…and it's good for the media to capture this…there's been no better and clearer direct line from corporate innovation, defense corporate innovation to the front lines than what's happened here at Ceramic. I've just seen it at CENTCOM. You've seen the way they've adapted in a dynamic environment and then put to use new technologies that, under a different Pentagon with a different mindset, may have taken years and years to develop and test and manufacture and QC (quality control). Instead, the idea is let's get this technology rapidly fielded to the front, where, A, we can use it and B, we can test it and then we can iterate on it because we've got members of the company forward with those fighting to get that feedback in real time to improve that product and use it more effectively next time. That is the feedback loop. That is the dynamic at all domains in which America will fight and fight successfully in the future. Whether it's in the Middle East, whether it's in our hemisphere, or whether it's in the Pacific, it will be real-time innovation with our best innovators and our best war fighters, out-innovating, out-scaling, out-competing our adversaries who just can't do what you do. They may try to copy it, or steal it, or replicate it in some way, but they can't do precisely what you do, and that is a decisive advantage for us. So, as I said, keep going. We see it, and we appreciate it every single day. God bless this great country, and God bless the Republic of Texas as well. Thank you.

title: Meritocracy at Center of Military Service, Hegseth Tells Cadets at Texas A&M
text: At Texas A&M University in College Station, Texas, today, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth told future officers that the U.S. military they will enter places a premium on meritocracy, and that once they put on their uniforms, they will march into formations that value them only for what they bring to the fight. 23:05 "Under the leadership of our commander in chief, President Donald J. Trump, our doctrine is clear: America first and peace through strength," Hegseth said. "And we achieve it in three distinct ways: reviving the warrior ethos, rebuilding our military and reestablishing deterrence here at home and across the globe." The secretary said that he knew restoring the warrior ethos also meant establishing a military centered on meritocracy rather than non-merit factors. "Two days after taking office, I signed the memorandum restoring America's fighting force," he said. "That directive established a bedrock standard that will guide your entire military service ... the armed forces of the United States will be governed strictly by merit, competence and combat readiness." The War Department, he said, is colorblind, gender-neutral and merit-based. "The only thing that matters are our standards, discipline, readiness, training and lethality," he said. "And we will never compromise on those standards." Walking onto the campus this morning, Hegseth said he was impressed by what he saw. "I do not see an academic institution trying to apologize for American strength; I see backbone and resolve, and the uncompromising future of the United States and the United States armed forces," he said. "I see a real, grounded, strong institution, which is exactly what our nation needs." The secretary's visit to Texas A&M University was part of a two-day trip. Yesterday, he visited Saronic, a defense contractor that builds autonomous ocean-going drones — one of which was used to rescue two AH-64 Apache pilots off the coast of Oman. Later that day, he administered the oath of enlistment to dozens of recruits, and today, he administered the oath of office to ROTC cadets. The secretary said what he sees in Texas is the entire package of what's needed to rebuild the U.S. military. "Just down the road, innovators are forging unmanned vessels, autonomous systems, drones, hypersonic missiles that will define modern deterrence," Hegseth said. "But standing right here in College Station, I'm looking at the indispensable other half of that equation: the future warfighters. ... The arsenal of freedom builds the sword right here in Texas, but that blade will be wielded as it always has been, by the Aggies standing in front of me today." The secretary reminded cadets that during World War II, more than 20,000 Aggies served, and that their school provided more leaders to the U.S. military than any other source outside the U.S. service academies. The same remains true today, he said. Not all of the men and women in the Texas A&M Corps of Cadets will go on to join the U.S. military — about 40% eventually accept a commission to serve. But those who do choose to serve, Hegseth said, will become part of the proud military history of the school. For those men and women, he said, he promised to always give them what they need so they can be best equipped to serve as they have sworn to do. "I make you this personal pledge: just as my fellow soldiers had my back on the battlefield in Iraq and Afghanistan, I will always have your back," he said. "And you can know that our commander in chief has your back every single day." Hegseth said his job at the Pentagon is to get them the weaponry, training, technology, and mission clarity they need to fight, win and then get home. He promised to do that. "We will never tie your hands behind your back; silly rules of engagement are gone. Warfighters are unleashed, and we [will] never ask you to apologize for being warriors," he said. "We will demand excellence, and at the same time, back you to the hilt. So, train hard, demand more of yourselves than anyone else would ever dare demand of you, uphold the honor of that uniform ... honor the memory of the Aggies who marched before you ... [and] prepare to lead the most formidable fighting force the world has ever known." title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Lower Drug Prices for All 50 State Medicaid Programs
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Lower Drug Prices for All 50 State Medicaid Programs The White House September 18, 2026 ADVANCING MOST-FAVORED-NATION (MFN) PRICING IN MEDICAID: Today, President Donald J. Trump announced that all 50 States’ Medicaid programs will benefit from lower prescription drug prices under his agreements with pharmaceutical manufacturers to match the lowest prices paid by other developed nations (known as the most-favored-nation, or MFN, prices). Under the GENEROUS Medicaid Payment Model, participating pharmaceutical manufacturers will provide State Medicaid programs with rebates on expensive brand-name drugs to ensure the final price to Medicaid does not exceed the MFN price. The model includes hundreds of individual drugs, across virtually all major drug classes, including those acutely important to Medicaid beneficiaries like oncology, diabetes care, and asthma. Due to the President’s MFN deals, Medicaid programs have already benefitted from one million free prescriptions of Eliquis, a widely used drug for heart disease. SAVING TAXPAYER DOLLARS WHILE MAINTAINING COVERAGE FOR THE MOST VULNERABLE: The Council of Economic Advisers has estimated that taxpayers will save $64.3B over the next decade in the form of lower Medicaid drug costs for all 50 States. As Medicaid costs are shared by both States and the Federal government, CEA estimates that $36.6B in savings will accrue to the Federal government and $27.6B to State governments. These savings will unlock significant capital for States to invest in other initiatives to better care for their most vulnerable residents. President Trump’s MFN agreements not only include lower prices for Medicaid, but also lower drug prices for direct-to-consumer purchases through TrumpRx.gov , guaranteeing MFN prices on all new innovative medicines brought to market and direct lower prices for consumers in the United States. LOWERING COSTS FOR AMERICANS: President Trump’s decisive and historic actions are lowering drug prices for the American people and ending pharmaceutical companies’ practice of charging American patients up to three times more than patients in other developed nations for the same drug. Since its February launch, patients have saved more than $700 million on medicines through TrumpRx.gov , including massive discounts on popular medications used to treat obesity and infertility. In July of 2026, senior citizens without access to GLP-1 coverage to treat obesity gained access for just $50 per month. In the two months since the launch of this program, 600,000 seniors have saved a total of $216 million dollars on these life-changing medicines. The Council of Economic Advisors estimates the total savings from President Trump’s MFN deals to reach $600 billion over the next decade. DELIVERING ON PROMISES TO PUT AMERICAN PATIENTS FIRST: President Trump is delivering on promises for American patients, accomplishing historic wins that the political establishment did not believe were possible. On May 12, 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order titled: “Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients” directing the Administration to take numerous actions to bring American drug prices in line with those paid by similar nations. On July 31, 2025, President Trump sent letters to 17 of the leading pharmaceutical manufacturers outlining the steps they must take to bring down the prices of prescription drugs in the United States to match the lowest price offered in other developed nations. There are now MFN deals with each of those leading pharmaceutical manufacturers. On September 30, 2025, President Trump announced the first agreement, with the drug manufacturer Pfizer, to bring MFN prices to American patients. On December 1, 2025, the Office of the United States Trade Representative, the Department of Commerce, and the Department of Health and Human Services announced an agreement with the United Kingdom (U.K.) that will increase the net price of new prescription drugs by 25% in the U.K., helping ensure they pay their fair share for innovative medicines. On December 19, 2025, President Trump announced nine new agreements with major pharmaceutical companies. On February 5, 2026, President Trump launched TrumpRx.gov , where patients can access large discounts on many of the most popular and highest-priced medicines in the country, paying prices in line with the MFN price. On August 31, 2026, President Trump announced nine new agreements with pharmaceutical manufacturers to lower prescription drug prices for Americans in line with the MFN price. As of today, the Administration has agreements with 26 pharmaceutical manufacturers, covering 89% of the branded drug market. Those manufacturers are Pfizer, Astra Zeneca, EMD Serono, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Bristol Myers Squibb, Boehringer Ingelheim, Genentech, Gilead Sciences, GSK, Merck, Novartis, Sanofi, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Regeneron, Alcon, Astellas Pharma, BeOne Medicines, BridgeBio, CSL, Kyowa Kirin, Sun Pharma, Teva Pharmaceuticals, and UCB. President Trump is calling on Congress to enact the Great Healthcare Plan , a comprehensive plan to lower drug prices, lower insurance premiums, hold big insurance companies accountable, and maximize price transparency.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Further Enhances Program Integrity and Interagency Coordination in the H-1B Visa Program
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Further Enhances Program Integrity and Interagency Coordination in the H-1B Visa Program The White House September 18, 2026 PROTECTING AMERICAN JOBS: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order and a Proclamation to continue to protect American national and economic security and American workers from abuses of the H-1B visa program. The Order enhances program integrity in the H-1B visa program by improving interagency coordination and directing enhanced scrutiny of H-1B visa applications where there is a heightened risk that American workers would be laid off. The Order directs the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Labor, and the Secretary of Homeland Security to consult with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Education, and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration in order to receive additional data for the administration of the H-1B program, such as data on wages, industrial conditions, and employment specialization. The Order directs the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Labor, and the Secretary of Homeland Security to consider petitioner employers’ recent or planned layoffs of similarly situated U.S. workers when considering H-1B visa applications. The Proclamation renews the $100,000 fee requirement for certain alien H-1B visa applications first imposed on September 19, 2025 to curb abuses that displace U.S. workers and undermine national security. COMBATTING H-1B ABUSES : President Trump’s 2025 Proclamation effectively deterred abuses in the H-1B visa program, and further action will ensure American workers are not replaced with lower-paid foreign labor. Since the 2025 Proclamation took effect, H-1B registrations filed by the largest IT outsourcing firms have been reduced by 92%. Before the 2025 Proclamation, unemployment among recent computer science graduates reached 6.1% and 7.5% for computer engineering graduates – more than double the rates for biology or art history majors. The number of foreign STEM workers in the United States had more than doubled between 2000 and 2019, while overall STEM employment only increased 44.5% during that time. The share of IT workers with H-1B visas had risen from 32% in FY 2003 to over 65% in recent years before the 2025 Proclamation. The Proclamation has also caused a nearly 97% decrease in consular processing requests and a shift from lower-paid foreign labor toward higher-skilled and higher-wage workers. More work must be done to improve interagency coordination in the assessment of H-1B visa petitions. Abuse of the H-1B visa program decreases wages for skilled American workers because the availability of cheaper foreign labor places downward pressure on domestic pay. Many employers have laid off large numbers of highly qualified, highly skilled American workers, only to promptly hire large numbers of H-1B workers who are often lower-skilled and lower-paid. Due to the outsourcing business model of certain H-1B sponsors, many jobs held by H-1B workers eventually leave the United States entirely. PUTTING AMERICAN WORKERS FIRST AND RESTORING THE IMMIGRATION SYSTEM: After years and years of failed policies that put foreigners above America’s own workers, President Trump has delivered on his promise to put American workers first and fix the immigration system. Since returning to office, President Trump’s economic policies have added over one million jobs to the U.S economy, including nearly 100,000 factory construction jobs and 58,000 manufacturing jobs since January 2026. President Trump ignited a manufacturing renaissance, with the U.S. manufacturing sector expanding for eight straight months after perpetual contraction in the Biden Administration. In July 2025, President Trump signed the largest tax cuts for working Americans in history which delivered No Tax on Overtime and No Tax on Tips, safeguarded millions of American jobs and over half a trillion dollars in wages, and established the first-ever Workforce Pell Grants for Americans in skilled trades. Under President Trump, real wages increased by $822 in 2025 and real household income reached its highest level in history after falling by thousands of dollars under the Biden Administration. The Trump Administration is cracking down on visa worker abuse and protecting American workers from being replaced with cheap foreign labor, including H-1B visa fraud investigations and investigations into other practices that illegally favor visa holders over Americans. In December 2025, the Department of Homeland Security finalized a rule replacing the H-1B randomized lottery with a weighted system based on wage level to protect American workers’ wages, working conditions, and job opportunities. Fiscal year 2027 is the first time that the H-1B lottery has been decided by wage, not chance, and registrations dropped by almost 40%. The Trump Administration strengthened visa programs and their screenings and paused visa processing for 75 high-risk countries to protect the homeland and deter overstays. Immediately upon taking office, President Trump secured the border and ended the Biden Administration’s record-shattering illegal immigration into the U.S. The Trump Administration has deported over 3 million illegal aliens and for 15 straight months, no illegal aliens have been released into the country.
