title: Presidential Message on National Recovery Month
text: Briefings & Statements Presidential Message on National Recovery Month The White House September 2, 2026 During National Recovery Month, we celebrate the more than 23 million Americans who have found a pathway from addiction to recovery, we recognize those who have helped them reclaim their lives, and we renew our commitment to supporting those still struggling to find hope and healing. Throughout every community in America, the effects of drug and alcohol addiction are felt in the lives of families, friends, and neighbors. Today, 48.4 million Americans suffer from addiction, and 69,973 Americans died last year to overdose. Every American deserves to live free from the grip of addiction—and my Administration is wholly committed to making that possible by preventing drug use before it starts, providing treatment at the earliest opportunity, and helping more Americans lead engaged and productive lives in recovery. In January, I was proud to establish the Great American Recovery Initiative, coordinating a national response to the disease of addiction across government, healthcare, faith communities, and the private sector while fostering a culture that celebrates recovery. I also signed an Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets to make our communities safer and help homeless Americans access addiction and mental health services needed to rebuild their lives. I am directing the Food and Drug Administration to prioritize non-opioid options for chronic pain, and I signed the SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act to strengthen federal grant programs for treatment, overdose response, and mental health care. We are also stopping deadly drugs before they ever reach our shores. I signed the HALT Fentanyl Act into law, classifying all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs; formally designated major international drug cartels as foreign terrorist organizations; sealed our border; and empowered our brave Border Patrol and Armed Forces with the resources needed to carry out massive drug seizures to keep fentanyl off our streets. Recovery is a testament to the strength of the American Spirit and the promise of a second chance. This month, we stand with those on the road to recovery and the families and communities who support them along the way. Together, we will help more Americans break free from addiction and lead healthy, productive, and fulfilling lives.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Historic Oil Agreement to Secure American Energy Dominance and Drive Venezuela’s Economic Recovery
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Historic Oil Agreement to Secure American Energy Dominance and Drive Venezuela’s Economic Recovery The White House August 31, 2026 SECURING STABLE & LOW-COST OIL SUPPLY IN OUR HEMISPHERE: In the biggest oil deal in world history, President Donald J. Trump has secured U.S. majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela – vastly expanding our current U.S. territorial proven reserves of roughly 46 billion barrels. This deal secures our energy dominance for the next century—all at zero cost to the United States. The deal, signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, gives the U.S. government powerful governance rights, economic ownership, and guaranteed low-cost off-take from a new private Venezuelan oil champion, which will be the second-largest private oil company by reserves in the world: In connection with this agreement, the Venezuelan interim authorities have granted North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), a privately held oil company that is the second-largest private Venezuelan oil producer and a proven operator, 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels. At no cost to the American taxpayer, NABEP has granted the U.S. Department of War’s Office of Strategic Capital a 35% equity stake in its corporate parent, representing up to hundreds of billions in value and dividends for the United States. NABEP has granted the U.S. Department of State the right to purchase, at production cost, a guaranteed 20% of the off-take from all current and future fields NABEP will operate—ensuring a stable supply of low-cost oil that can facilitate refilling the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR), which Joe Biden depleted to historic lows, and to provide supply for military and other sensitive uses. NABEP has also granted the U.S. Department of State the right of first refusal to purchase the remaining 80% of its production, providing a guaranteed source of energy in our hemisphere in emergency situations. The U.S. government has a veto power over the appointment of any member of the board of directors, and a majority of NABEP’s board of directors must be U.S. citizens. NABEP will have reputable U.S. auditors, lawyers, and advisors and the U.S. government’s agreement with NABEP is governed by U.S. law and is subject to the jurisdiction of U.S. courts. Millions of barrels of new Venezuelan output will be processed through U.S. refineries and pumped with American rigs and infrastructure, supporting billions in investment in the United States and thousands of jobs here at home. DRIVING ECONOMIC RECOVERY & THE RECONSTRUCTION OF VENEZUELA’S OIL SECTOR: This groundbreaking privatization and investment in Venezuela’s energy sector is a key step in the Trump Administration’s three-part plan of stabilization, reconstruction and democratic transition. Private-sector led growth in production, output, and investment in Venezuela is a key precondition to driving continued reform and democratic transition following the incredible success of Operation Absolute Resolve: NABEP has developed an ambitious plan to rapidly scale production by investing up to $100 billion in new oil infrastructure in Venezuela, helping to drive economic growth, support thousands of high-paying jobs in Venezuela, and lead to tens of billions in broader economic activity. NABEP’s concessions are governed by Venezuela’s new hydrocarbons law, adopted with U.S. support, which provides for historic modernization, privatization and development of Venezuela’s lagging oil sector. Under this framework, as it scales production, NABEP will pay an expected $200 billion in royalty and tax payments over the first 25 years, representing critical revenue and fiscal support for current and future Venezuelan governments to fund reconstruction and social development. After years of underinvestment and mismanagement, the majority of Venezuela’s oil fields are not producing or vastly underproducing. By investing in a proven private operator with a track record of scaling production in the country, who will be able to raise private American capital to fund capital expenditures, Venezuela has a historic opportunity to revitalize its key sector, drive oil output growth, and grow its economy. The U.S. government’s robust governance and audit provisions, along with the Trump Administration’s banking reform, payment oversight and financial monitorship, will ensure tax and royalty payments are spent in the interests of the Venezuelan people. The United States is sponsoring reconciliation talks between the 2015 National Assembly and the interim authorities – a process which has already resulted in significant reforms to the Venezuelan judiciary, the release of hundreds of political prisoners, and cooperative efforts to finance reconstruction following the devastating June earthquakes. The process will continue with additional meetings in September. REASSERTING THE MONROE DOCTRINE & EXPELLING FOREIGN ADVERSARIES FROM OUR HEMISPHERE: The majority of the incremental oil fields to be operated by NABEP were previously controlled or operated by Russian and Chinese firms, or by corrupt cronies of Maduro and Chavez. These malign foreign actors looted Venezuela’s resources for the benefit of American adversaries like Cuba, Russia and China and failed to invest in Venezuela’s infrastructure or development. President Trump has re-established the Monroe Doctrine, purging foreign malign influence from our backyard and ensuring American dominance in our hemisphere is never again questioned. By working with both new and old partners, President Trump’s Administration is forging new robust, strategic and defensible supply chains in our hemisphere to support the revitalization of our manufacturing and energy sectors after years of globalist decline.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Deal with Nine Additional Pharmaceutical Manufacturers to Lower Drug Prices for Americans
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Deal with Nine Additional Pharmaceutical Manufacturers to Lower Drug Prices for Americans The White House August 31, 2026 ADVANCING MOST-FAVORED-NATION (MFN) PRICING: Today, President Donald J. Trump announced nine new agreements with pharmaceutical manufacturers to lower prescription drug prices for Americans in line with the lowest prices paid by other developed nations (known as the most-favored-nation, or MFN, price). The agreements bring the total number of pharmaceutical manufacturers with MFN deals to 26, covering 89% of the branded drug market. The nine manufacturers are comprised of mid-sized pharmaceutical companies, including Alcon, Astellas Pharma, BeOne Medicines, BridgeBio, CSL, Kyowa Kirin, Sun Pharma, Teva Pharmaceuticals, and UCB. The agreements reduce prices on drugs that treat numerous costly, chronic, and even rare diseases, including hemophilia, Parkinson’s disease, macular degeneration, glaucoma, liver disease, skin conditions, and various forms of cancer. The agreements will provide every State Medicaid program in the country access to MFN drug prices on products made by the nine companies, resulting in billions of dollars in savings for Americans and continuing President Trump’s historic efforts to strengthen the program for the most vulnerable. The agreements ensure foreign nations can no longer use price controls to freeride on American innovation by guaranteeing MFN prices on all new innovative medicines the nine companies bring to market. Each of these manufacturers has agreed to fundamentally rebalance international drug pricing by providing MFN pricing to American patients. BOLSTERING AMERICA’S PHARMACEUTICAL SUPPLY CHAINS AND RESERVES: These nine pharmaceutical manufacturers committed to invest at least $19.6 billion collectively in U.S. manufacturing in the near term. Additionally, as part of the MFN agreements, several companies are donating active pharmaceutical ingredients for key products to the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR) to reduce reliance on foreign nations and ensure the United States has an adequate supply of such products in the event of an emergency. UCB will contribute 163 tons of levetiracetam, an anticonvulsant used to control and prevent certain types of seizures, to the SAPIR. Sun Pharma will contribute 71.4 tons of clindamycin and 6.75 tons of doxycycline; both antibiotics to treat bacterial infections, to the SAPIR. Teva Pharmaceuticals will contribute 45 metric tons of metronidazole, an antibiotic and antiprotozoal used to treat certain bacterial and parasitic infections, and 4.8 tons of amlodipine, an antihypertensive drug, to the SAPIR. Astellas will contribute 25 kg of tacrolimus, an immunosuppressant used to prevent organ rejection in people who have had organ transplants, to the SAPIR. LOWERING COSTS FOR AMERICANS: President Trump’s decisive and historic actions are lowering drug prices for the American people. Since its February launch, patients have saved more than $700 million on medicines through TrumpRx, including massive discounts on some of the most popular and costly medications used to treat obesity and infertility. In July of 2026, senior citizens without access to GLP-1 coverage to treat obesity gained access for just $50 per month. In the two months since the launch of this program, over 500,000 seniors have saved a total of $216 million dollars on these life-changing medicines. The Council of Economic Advisers estimates the total savings from President Trump’s MFN deals to reach $600 billion over the next decade. DELIVERING ON PROMISES TO PUT AMERICAN PATIENTS FIRST: President Trump is delivering on promises for American patients, accomplishing historic wins that the political establishment did not believe were possible. On May 12, 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order titled: “Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients” directing the Administration to take numerous actions to bring American drug prices in line with those paid by similar nations. On July 31, 2025, President Trump sent letters to 17 of the leading pharmaceutical manufacturers outlining the steps they must take to bring down the prices of prescription drugs in the United States to match the lowest price offered in other developed nations. There are now MFN deals with each of those leading pharmaceutical manufacturers. On September 30, 2025, President Trump announced the first agreement, with the drug manufacturer Pfizer, to bring MFN prices to American patients. On December 1, 2025, the Office of the United States Trade Representative, the Department of Commerce, and the Department of Health and Human Services announced an agreement with the United Kingdom (U.K.) that will increase the net price of new prescription drugs by 25% in the U.K., helping ensure they pay their fair share for innovative medicines. On December 19, 2025, President Trump announced nine new agreements with major pharmaceutical companies. On February 5, 2026, President Trump launched TrumpRx.gov , where patients can access large discounts on many of the most popular and highest-priced medicines in the country, paying prices in line with the MFN price. As of today, August 31, the Administration now has agreements with Pfizer, Astra Zeneca, EMD Serono, Eli Lilly, Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Bristol Myers Squibb, Boehringer Ingelheim, Genentech, Gilead Sciences, GSK, Merck, Novartis, Sanofi, Johnson & Johnson, AbbVie, Regeneron, Alcon, Astellas Pharma, BeOne Medicines, BridgeBio, CSL, Kyowa Kirin, Sun Pharma, Teva Pharmaceuticals, and UCB. President Trump is calling on Congress to enact the Great Healthcare Plan , a comprehensive plan to lower drug prices, lower insurance premiums, hold big insurance companies accountable, and maximize price transparency.

title: Guard Program Links Global Partnership to DOW Priorities
text: Senior leaders and security cooperation personnel from across the War Department gathered for the 2026 National Guard Bureau State Partnership Program conference in Atlanta, Aug. 13. The goal of the annual conference was to align activities and engagements with National Defense Strategy Lines of Effort, administration arms transfer reform objectives and rigorous data-driven evaluation to prove return on investment for the American taxpayer. Combat Readiness Indiana National Guard soldiers assigned to the 1st Battalion, 151st Infantry Regiment, and Slovak Armed Forces soldiers conduct an assault on an objective during a combat readiness exercise near Butlerville, Ind., July 26, 2026. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.91 MB ) Credit: Army Staff Sgt. DeWayne Johnson VIRIN: 260726-Z-DT466-4123 In addition to DOW, the event included speakers from the Defense Security Cooperation Agency, Defense Security Cooperation University and the National Guard Bureau's International Affairs Directorate, including the assessment, monitoring and evaluation, foreign disclosure and integration teams. Throughout the event, speakers tied ongoing SPP achievements to the four NDS LOEs: defend the Homeland; deter China in the Pacific region through strength, not confrontation; increase burden-sharing with U.S. allies and partners; and supercharge the U.S. defense industrial base. Keynote speaker Christopher Mamaux, deputy assistant secretary of war for security cooperation, highlighted the program's critical role in operationalizing national security objectives. "As we look to the future, we must transition our partnerships from a default of security dependence to operational independence," Mamaux said. "We want to focus our energy on developing model allies, partners who are willing to spend on their own defense and contribute meaningfully to regional security." Mamaux emphasized the asymmetric advantage built over decades of state-level engagement. "With 117 partner nations, we have built a network of trust over decades that our strategic competitors cannot hope to replicate," he said. David Ferrari, the Defense Security Cooperation Agency advisor to the director, focused on the intersection of the SPP and the defense industrial ecosystem under Executive Order 14383, the America First Arms Transfer Strategy. Ferrari characterized guard personnel in the field as an "early-warning system" for foreign military sales requirements. "This is exactly where the SPP's persistent engagement is a strategic enabler, as you are in these countries year after year and can help partners identify what they need before they submit a request," he said, noting that this operational alignment creates a reinforcing cycle between procurement and capability development. "As we improve FMS processes to help partners buy more U.S. equipment, we are directly scaling the arena for SPP activities," Ferrari said. He concluded with a direct call to action for guard leaders to leverage partner investment to strengthen mutual readiness. Partnership Program Air Force Senior Master Sgt. Steven Dauck, a flight chief assigned to Hawaii Air National Guard's 154th Explosive Ordnance Disposal Flight, shows an OG-9 recoilless training weapon to Indonesian Air Force personnel at Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, July 22, 2026. Hawaii National Guard service members routinely train with their Indonesian Air Force counterparts through the State Partnership Program, which aims to enhance disaster response, aviation, medical readiness, cybersecurity and professional development between the partner nations. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.82 MB ) Credit: Air Force Senior Airman Roann Gatdula VIRIN: 260722-Z-KH177-1003 "As you conduct your persistent engagements this year, look at your partners through the lens of [the America First Arms Transfer Strategy]," he said. "Help us identify where partner capital can invest in mutual capacity, and help us transition them to modern, standard U.S. systems. We cannot reindustrialize the arsenal of freedom without the guard leading the way on the ground." Regarding workforce development, Sonya Finley, the dean of workforce education and development at the Defense Security Cooperation University, outlined key milestones in the professionalization of security cooperation. Under DSCU, the SPP has been officially designated as a distinct functional area within the War Department's Security Cooperation Workforce Certification 2.0 Program — a major step toward codifying and standardizing global partnership management across the joint force. Conference sessions also underscored the importance of maintaining high-quality data processes. Recent policy guidance has institutionalized assessment, monitoring and evaluation as a mandatory mechanism to measure performance, demonstrate accountability and justify resourcing for SPP activities. Mamaux reinforced that strategic alignment applies directly to resource stewardship. "We must prove that our resources are aligned with the NDS lines of effort and provide a very clear return on our investment," he said. "Every dollar you spend across the program must be logical, transparent and benefit the American people." Partners in the Skies Air Force Staff Sgt. Jack Heintz, a crew chief assigned to the New York Air National Guard's 106th Maintenance Squadron, describes the capabilities of an HC-130J Combat King II aircraft to Swedish Air Force Cpl. Wincent Enhörning, a helicopter mechanic assigned to Malmen Air Base in Linköping, Sweden, Aug. 20, 2026. New York National Guard members are in Sweden for events surrounding the Swedish Air Force's centennial jubilee and engagements through the National Guard State Partnership Program. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 409.6 KB ) Credit: Army Sgt. 1st Class Christy Sherman VIRIN: 260821-A-AW306-7609 Presenters highlighted real-world examples of guard activities that have delivered strategic outcomes. In one instance, military planners maximized space on existing training transport to deliver equipment to Albania, achieving a critical delivery while eliminating commercial transportation costs. In another example of interstate collaboration, when Bulgaria's state partner, the Tennessee National Guard, identified a requirement for Stryker platforms outside its force structure, it coordinated with the Washington National Guard to fill the gap seamlessly. Regarding the program's future expansion, Mamaux noted that growth will remain deliberate and value driven. "Under our current strategic policy, we anticipate accepting only two to three new partnerships per year," he said. "Every pairing must offer a clear benefit to United States national security interests and align with the NDS." Experience: Building Partnerships Around the Globe

title: Army Lasers Blast Drones, Proving Directed-Energy Weapons Are Future
text: Protecting the Homeland Joint Task Force Southern Border personnel use the Army Multipurpose High Energy Laser system to engage and defeat three hostile unmanned aerial systems along the U.S. southern border, Aug. 25, 2026. Approximately 8,000 service members are currently deployed as part of the task force to protect U.S. territorial integrity by boosting awareness, accelerating response and supporting federal law enforcement partners. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 389.12 KB ) Credit: Army Sgt. Daniel Huerta VIRIN: 260826-D-D0945-3729 Earlier this week, service members assigned to Joint Task Force Southern Border used the Army Multipurpose High Energy Laser system to stop three hostile, unmanned aircraft systems deemed a threat. They were believed to be linked to drug cartels. "The successful defeat of these adversarial drones is a direct testament to the readiness, vigilance and technological edge of the [joint task force]," said Army Maj. Gen. Curtis Taylor, Joint Task Force Southern Border commander. "By integrating layered countermeasures alongside advanced directed-energy capabilities like this laser system, we have made it clear that we will not tolerate hostile surveillance." The operation marks the first use of the laser system to defeat cartel-linked drones along the southern border. Using directed-energy weapons, such as this, is part of the future of warfare, a War Department official said. "The future of warfare obviously is going to include mass attritable drones," the official added. The department will procure hundreds of thousands of drones as soon as next year, as well as counter-UAS technology, including directed-energy systems. "The department is proliferating directed-energy technology to protect the homeland and the southern border," the official said. "And [U.S. Northern Command and Joint Task Force Southern Border are] deploying these capabilities to take out any ... cartel drones that are doing incursions at the border." Directed-energy weapons, such as lasers, can be used to take out both drones and incoming cruise missiles, at a much lower cost than using more expensive kinetic weapons like missiles. Developing scaled directed energy weapons systems, such as what was used at the border, is one of the department's six critical technology areas. The other areas include: applied artificial intelligence, biomanufacturing, contested logistics technologies, quantum and battlefield information dominance, and scaled hypersonics. "[Directed-energy systems are] low cost per shot, with deep magazines and they can come out against drone swarms," the official said. "That's something that's different than a traditional kinetic system. It's good for the cost-exchange ratio because ... it's better than us firing a $2 million missile at [an inexpensive] drone." The use of directed-energy weapons on drones is also in line with the department's counter-drone effort, the official noted. By integrating layered countermeasures alongside advanced directed-energy capabilities like this laser system, we have made it clear that we will not tolerate hostile surveillance." Army Maj. Gen. Curtis Taylor, Joint Task Force Southern Border commander In June, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth visited White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico, where he observed a variety of directed-energy systems in operation, including the first milestone test of the Golden Dome for America. "Cutting-edge directed energy was harnessed, and the Dynamic Defense Autonomous Defeat system flawlessly and autonomously cued, targeted and eliminated a multitude of incoming threats," the secretary said. "This test was executed on schedule and dynamically defeated every threat. I watched our elite warfighters integrate with next-generation technology to stop incoming drones and cruise missiles dead in their tracks." In July, the War Department awarded two agreements under the Joint Laser Weapon System program to advance the next-generation cruise missile and unmanned aerial system defense architecture. The agreements have an initial award value of $86 million and a total program ceiling of $847 million. The Joint Laser Weapon System program is meant to transition directed-energy capabilities from demonstration prototypes into field-ready, production-oriented platforms. "We must actively defend the homeland against emerging threats," said Emil Michael, undersecretary of war for research and engineering and chief technology officer for the War Department. "We are partnering with industry to rapidly deliver deep magazine directed energy capabilities to the joint force that can be seamlessly deployed across multiple domains." title: Sky Soldiers Train for Modern Conflict in Europe's Premier Crucible Event
text: More than 2,300 paratroopers assigned to the 173rd Airborne Brigade, along with more than 2,100 allied and partner forces from 10 nations are participating in Exercise Saber Junction 26 at the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, Germany. Saber Junction A soldier assigned to Joint Multinational Readiness Center's Cherokee Company, 1st Battalion, 4th Infantry Regiment, pulls security during Exercise Saber Junction 26 at the Joint Multinational Readiness Center's Hohenfels Training Area in Germany, Aug. 26, 2026. Collin Mackall, 7th Army Training Command VIRIN: 260826-A-XV403-1019 Overseen by U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa, the rotation is designed to validate warfighting readiness, strengthen NATO interoperability and prepare forces for large-scale combat operations across the European theater. Exercise Saber Junction 26 tests the brigade's ability to rapidly deploy, conduct joint forcible entry, execute offensive and defensive operations, and regenerate combat power in a contested environment. The exercise incorporates lessons learned from ongoing conflicts, including electronic warfare, unmanned aerial systems, dispersed maneuver and contested communications. Southern European Task Force, Africa serves as the division-level higher command for the rotation, integrating U.S. and allied formations, issuing division orders, maintaining the common operating picture, and rehearsing mission command essential for operations across Europe and Africa. "Saber Junction is where our soldiers and our allies prove they are ready for the demands of modern war," said Army Maj. Gen. Matthew W. Brown, Southern European Task Force, Africa commander. "This rotation is a crucible event — designed to expose gaps, accelerate learning and ensure that formations are trained and lethal. The 173rd continues to demonstrate that disciplined application of the fundamentals, ground-up innovation and persistence remain the hallmarks of a combat-credible force. The brigade is ready — and the lessons we gather here help our Army scale innovation at pace and strengthen NATO's collective readiness." {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} - {{slideCaption}} Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( {{filesize}} ) Credit: {{photographer}} VIRIN: {{virin}} {{slideNumber}} of {{numSlides}} {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideTitle}} - {{slideCaption}} {{slideInfo.slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideInfo.slideTitle}} - {{slideInfo.slideCaption}} The exercise also highlights modernization efforts within the 173rd Airborne Brigade, including the work of the bayonet innovation team, the brigade's internal innovation cell comprised of paratroopers, engineers, warrant officers and technical specialists. The team designs, builds and fields low-cost, high-impact technologies such as first-person view drones, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance platforms, ground robots and artificial intelligence-enabled tools. It operates a facility that can produce drones in-house and integrates lessons from Ukraine, Joint Multinational Readiness Center rotations and multinational exercises to help the brigade adapt rapidly and strengthen NATO interoperability. "Our standards are nonnegotiable: disciplined, lethal and relentless. Saber Junction is where we put those expectations to the test," said Army Col. Mark E. Bush, 173rd Airborne Brigade commander. Through the character, competence and commitment of our Sky Soldiers, we will deliver overwhelming firepower, maneuver aggressively and accomplish the mission alongside our allies." Exercise Saber Junction 26 includes participants from Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Kosovo, Lithuania, Poland, Ukraine, and the United States. The exercise strengthens multinational interoperability and accelerates combined decision making across the European theater. title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Further Ensures Affordable Beef for the American Consumer
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Further Ensures Affordable Beef for the American Consumer The White House August 26, 2026 ADDRESSING BEEF AFFORDABILITY WITH TARGETED ACTION: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed a Proclamation to temporarily increase the quantity of lean beef trimmings that are imported with no above-quota tariff to ensure affordable beef for American consumers in light of current supply challenges. This action includes key safeguards to maximize cost savings while protecting American ranchers from foreign imports and giving space for American ranchers to grow the domestic herd. The Proclamation temporarily expands the existing quantity of lean beef trimmings that are subject to an in-quota tariff rate, to produce ground beef, allowing trading partners eligible to ship beef to the United States to take advantage of lower, in-quota tariff rates. This expanded quota has the following limitations: It only applies for 90 days, beginning on September 1, 2026. It only allows 100,000 tons per month. (USDA projects U.S. beef production in 2026 to be over 11 million tons.) It only applies to lean beef trimmings to combine with U.S. beef for ground beef. It encourages beef to be sold at a 25% discount from the going import price. The Proclamation does not modify any commitments related to beef for countries with a free trade agreement with the United States, and does not apply to countries with country-specific beef quotas. FURTHER RESPONDING TO REDUCED U.S. BEEF AVAILABILITY AND HIGHER DOMESTIC DEMAND: President Trump is taking decisive action to respond to market disruptions and natural disasters in order to ensure adequate supply and affordable prices of beef products for American families. The Biden Administration put American agriculture last and delivered one of its most severe beef supply crises in decades, with domestic cattle herds at their lowest level in 75 years. Years of pursuing radical climate activists’ misguided policies and inciting inflation that left farmers with historically high input costs put enormous pressure on American agriculture and the ranchers who feed our country. The Trump Administration has been working around the clock to help rebuild the American beef industry – for the first time since 2018, the number of cattle in the U.S. is increasing and ranchers are retaining heifers at higher rates. Since President Trump’s Proclamation in February addressing the elevated beef prices for U.S. consumers, including the elevated price of ground beef, many factors—including necessary restrictions on live animal imports from Mexico in order to mitigate the spread of the New World Screwworm, drought conditions across cattle-producing regions affecting grazing lands, and reduced feed and forage availability due to ongoing wildfire conditions—have put downward pressure on the size of the U.S. domestic herd. For example, the necessary closure of southern ports in response to the New World Screwworm to protect the American herd resulted in a loss of hundreds of thousands of metric tons of beef being produced in the United States. As a result of these and other factors, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) forecasts U.S. beef output will fall by around four percent from 2025 levels. The United States is the world’s largest consumer of beef by volume and ranks second globally in per capita beef consumption, underscoring beef’s importance to the American diet. As Americans eat more beef than ever, it is necessary and appropriate to ensure that the supply of beef products will be sufficient to meet U.S. demand at affordable and reasonable prices. The President is taking temporary action to strengthen the Nation’s supply of affordable beef for American consumers while these supply challenges persist. This temporary action will increase beef supply by roughly 10% over current projections – an amount that will deliver economic relief to American consumers, will only compete with cull cow markets, and will not significantly impact the fed cattle market. This action will not make up for the entire quantity of beef that would have been in the U.S. marketplace without the necessary closure of the U.S. – Mexican border to delay the incursion of New World Screwworm. President Trump continues to support and uplift America’s ranchers as they rebuild from years of neglect from the Biden Administration. DELIVERING LOWER COSTS FOR AMERICAN FAMILIES WHILE SUPPORTING OUR RANCHERS: Since returning to office, President Trump has moved swiftly to restore affordability, fight to reverse the Biden Administration’s inflation crisis, and strengthen America’s farmers, ranchers, and food supply. Under four years of Biden, workers lost nearly $3,000 in purchasing power—meaning inflation rose faster than wages. Under President Trump, even after accounting for higher prices, real wages grew by $822 in 2025, putting more money in the pockets of hard-working Americans, with more savings on the way from further deregulation. From day one, President Trump began halting proposed Biden-era regulations, which have saved Americans over $211 billion, or $2,461 per family of four. In July 2025, President Trump signed the largest tax cuts in American history, providing families with thousands more in their pockets each year. The Working Families Tax Cuts various tax provisions, such as the now-permanent small-business deduction and death tax exemption, and the first increase in reference prices in over 10 years, make the ranching industry more attractive for investment, boosting profitability for ranchers now and into the future. Since taking office, the Trump Administration began implementing a robust plan to protect the American herd from the threat of New World Screwworm. Certain southern ports remain closed to live animal imports from Mexico as the United States pursues a phased and monitored reopening to increase the beef supply with robust, overlapping safeguards. In October 2025, the Trump Administration announced a suite of actions to strengthen the American beef industry, reinforcing and prioritizing the American rancher’s critical role in the national security of the United States. In December 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to stop price fixing, anti-competitive behavior, and foreign influence that drives up grocery prices and threatens the security of America’s food supply. In February 2026, President Trump issued a proclamation to temporarily increase imports and reduce beef prices for American consumers. In June 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order to accelerate American agriculture innovation, empowering farmers and ranchers and bolstering the strength and security of our food supply. Today’s action reflects The Trump Administration’s continued focus on driving down costs for all Americans. The Trump Administration has strengthened the farm safety net, expanded crop insurance, cut red tape, and reduced costs for farmers. President Trump is committed to reducing risk for cattle producers, supporting new ranchers across the country, and ensuring ranchers are prosperous now and into the future.

title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Declares a National Emergency to Secure America’s Bulk-Power System
text: Fact Sheets Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Declares a National Emergency to Secure America’s Bulk-Power System The White House August 26, 2026 SECURING AMERICA’S BULK-POWER SYSTEM: Today, President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order to protect the security, integrity, and reliability of bulk-power system electric equipment used in the United States, particularly from interference by foreign actors. The Order declares a national emergency under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act with respect to the unusual and extraordinary foreign threat to the United States involving bulk-power systems produced abroad that may present national security vulnerabilities. To deal with the threat to the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States, the Order, among other things, generally prohibits certain foreign-produced bulk-power system electric equipment, including associated critical software and digital capabilities that could pose cybersecurity or operational risks, from being purchased or installed in the United States, or appropriately conditions such purchases and installations to address those risks. The Order focuses on transactions involving foreign nationals that pose an undue risk of sabotage, unauthorized access, or other disruption, an undue risk of catastrophic effects on the security or resiliency of U.S. critical infrastructure, or an unacceptable risk to the security of the U.S. The Order does not apply to facilities used for local distribution of electric energy. The Order further permits the Secretary of Energy, in consultation with other members of the Cabinet, to impose conditions on the continued use and operation of such equipment as needed to address the concerns identified in the Order, bearing in mind effects on reliability, safety, availability of replacements, and continuity of service. The Order directs the Secretary of Energy to publish rules operationalizing and implementing the Order as needed. The Order further directs the Secretary of Energy, in consultation with other members of the Cabinet, to identify bulk-power system electric equipment that may pose risks identified in the Order and prepare recommendations for the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs to address the risks posed by that equipment. PREVENTING FOREIGN ACTORS FROM CRIPPLING CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE: President Trump is taking steps to eliminate supply chain vulnerabilities while ensuring abundant, reliable electricity. The rapid growth of advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, and defense production has increased America’s dependence on certain foreign components necessary for the provision of abundant, reliable electricity. Continued reliance on foreign sources of bulk-power system electric equipment creates a supply chain vulnerability to the U.S. Current minimal restrictions on acquisition or operation of foreign-produced bulk-power system electric equipment augment the ability of some foreign entities to create and exploit vulnerabilities in such equipment. Certain foreign actors are increasingly creating and exploiting vulnerabilities in the United States bulk-power system, which provides the electricity that supports our national defense, vital emergency services, critical infrastructure, and the economy. SECURING AMERICA’S CRITICAL SUPPLY CHAINS: President Trump has long recognized that America’s national security and economic strength depend on rebuilding key sectors of our industrial base and their supply chains. In his first term, President Trump revolutionized international trade by using Section 232 to address decades of short-sighted, globalist trade policies that hollowed out our domestic steel and aluminum industries. Since returning to office, President Trump has continued taking actions under Section 232 to protect and strengthen domestic manufacturing critical to our national and economic security, including imposing and strengthening tariffs on key goods such as steel, aluminum, copper, polysilicon, trucks, automobiles, timber, lumber, semiconductors, and pharmaceuticals. In April 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to strengthen and secure the United States electric grid. This resulted in 17,000 megawatts (MW) — enough electricity to supply power to 12.75 million homes — of perfectly good power plants from being forced offline due to weaponization of state and Federal environmental regulations, reducing costs for consumers and enhancing grid reliability. In June 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order to advance American AI innovation to strengthen America’s cybersecurity, protect critical infrastructure, and ensure the United States remains the global leader in AI innovation. In July 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order to secure America’s defense supply chains for the cutting-edge equipment that allows the U.S. to dominate the modern battlefield, particularly, the critical materials and components necessary to manufacture that equipment. In August 2026, President Trump signed a Proclamation to address the national security threat posed by imports of drones and their components, including by strengthening America’s drone industry and supply chain.

title: Review Panel Continues Its Mission as Pentagon Marks Fifth Anniversary of Abbey Gate Bombing
text: Senior Advisor to the Secretary of War Sean Parnell revealed in a social media post today that an ongoing War Department investigation into the circumstances surrounding the 2021 terrorist airport bombing in Kabul, Afghanistan, has uncovered classified documents that had not been previously located. Airport Security Army paratroopers assigned to the 1st Brigade Combat Team, 82nd Airborne Division, conduct security as they facilitate the evacuation of U.S. citizens, special immigrant visa applicants and other at-risk Afghans out of Afghanistan as quickly and safely as possible at Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul, Aug. 25, 2021. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 4.7 MB ) Credit: Army Master Sgt. Alexander Burnett VIRIN: 210825-A-UV471-113A Parnell gave the update on the fifth anniversary of the suicide bombing attack at then-Hamid Karzai International Airport's Abbey Gate, which killed 13 U.S. service members and approximately 170 Afghan civilians. "Recently, my team recovered highly relevant classified documents — material that should have been disclosed — stashed and hidden away in safes where they would not be found," Parnell said, adding that, once the documents were discovered and examined by a special review panel, "it became clear why someone tried to hide them." An update from Sean Parnell, Chairman of the Afghanistan Withdrawal Special Review Panel, on the Fifth Anniversary of the Abbey Gate bombing pic.twitter.com/5pkbmuuyX0 — Sean Parnell (@SeanParnellASW) August 26, 2026 Parnell went on to say that he didn't want to disclose the contents of the classified documents prematurely. "I'm not going to give you a convenient version of the truth, nor will I give you a rushed one. Here is my commitment: We are following the evidence to wherever it leads and to whoever it touches. We're not accepting incomplete or comfortable answers," he said. One year ago, on the fourth anniversary of the attack and while surrounded by Gold Star family members of the victims in the Oval Office, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced that Parnell — himself a veteran of the war in Afghanistan — had been selected to lead the special review panel looking into the attack and that the ongoing review was taking place on behalf of the American people and on behalf of the Gold Star families. Thirteen Roses Thirteen roses, two pink and eleven white, rest on the pedestal of the United States Marine Corps War Memorial in Arlington, Va., Aug. 28, 2021, representing the thirteen U.S. service members who lost their lives while assisting non-combatant evacuation screening at Abbey Gate of Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul, Afghanistan. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.68 MB ) Credit: Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Kelly L. Timney VIRIN: 210828-M-OU200-1052 "America deserves answers as far as what happened in Afghanistan," Hegseth said. "The military needs to answer for what happened." During his address on social media, Parnell spoke highly of the panel members, noting that they have extensive military service in Afghanistan. "These patriots commanded troops; they took fire; they carried the wounded, and they buried their friends," he said. "They knew how decisions in Afghanistan became consequences because they are the ones who lived with them." Airport Security An Afghan man hands his child to a British paratrooper assigned to the 2nd Battalion, Parachute Regiment, while a U.S. service member assigned to the Army's 1st Brigade Combat Team, 82nd Airborne Division, conducts security at Hamid Karzai International Airport in Kabul, Afghanistan, Aug. 26, 2021. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 3.97 MB ) Credit: Army Master Sgt. Alexander Burnett VIRIN: 210826-A-UV471-211 The establishment of the special review panel followed U.S. Central Command's supplemental review in April 2024, which revisited the military's original investigation into the attack. That review, which identified the lone suicide attacker as a member of ISIS-Khorasan, determined the initial investigation's findings were accurate: that the attack could not have been prevented at the tactical level. Though Parnell did not give a specific timeframe as to when he anticipates the special review panel's work being completed, he did ensure the thoroughness and integrity of its investigation. "The American people and the families who sacrificed everything are owed the full picture of how and why those decisions were made, and we're going to give it to them," he said. "That's a promise — not just for today, not just for an anniversary — but until it's done."

title: Army Armaments Center Unveils New Ammo Packaging System
text: Blending lightweight polymers with a rugged steel shell, the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center's new SixPAC system marks a groundbreaking leap in small-caliber ammunition packaging, one intended to reshape how soldiers use munitions. The SixPAC, named for its capacity to hold 6.8 mm cartridges, consists of two lightweight polymer ammunition containers in a steel outer pack. After successful implementation with the cartridges, the system is planned for adaptation across multiple legacy small-caliber ammunition production lines. New SixPAC The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center's next-generation lightweight packaging system, the SixPAC, is built to modernize small-caliber ammunition logistics and reduce weight, costs and supply chain vulnerabilities. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 102.4 KB ) Credit: Eric Kowal, Army VIRIN: 260825-A-GY890-1001 This initiative serves as the first major overhaul of small-caliber ammunition packaging since World War II. Supply chain vulnerabilities, rising costs and a need to prepare for tomorrow's military operations in varied climates necessitated a reevaluation of current munitions packaging. The system is designed with a lighter tactical inner pack, which will broaden its manufacturing base and increase efficiency. The system is defined by the absence of a traditional outer wood box, which often required remediation, had to be assembled manually and was susceptible to mold. It also reduces reliance on chemical wood preservative treatments, lowering environmental impacts and the risk of supply chain disruption. The polymer inner pack reduces weight, enables easier transport and is more efficient to manufacture. The steel outer pack reduces the logistical footprint by allowing more containers and ammunition per pallet and has a notably larger supply base than its legacy wood counterpart. Crucible Training Kyesha T. Siggers, a Marine Corps recruit assigned to Bravo Company, 1st Recruit Training Battalion, passes an ammo can over an obstacle during the crucible training event at Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island, S.C., July 30, 2026. The crucible is the final culminating event recruits must complete before earning the title of Marine. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 1.37 MB ) Credit: Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Katrina Wallace VIRIN: 260730-M-UA605-1239 Teamwork Makes the Dream Work Marine Corps recruit Kyesha T. Siggers passes an ammo can through an obstacle during the Crucible at Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island, S.C., July 30, 2026. The Crucible is the final culminating event recruits must complete before earning the title of Marine. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 6 MB ) Credit: Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Katrina Wallace VIRIN: 260730-M-UA605-9612 According to the project's technical lead, Jason Runell, the SixPAC was partly driven by a desire to do away with the wooden box and largely pursued to modernize for present-day logistics, portability and supply chain challenges. His team tested several materials and received feedback from various user communities before landing on a polymer inner pack and a steel outer pack. This decision, he added, comes out of necessity — polymers aren't yet as proven in the U.S. as they are in other countries. However, the U.S. must be ready to engage at any time and fight in various climates, all with their own difficulties and needs. To meet military standards, polymers must hold up no matter the locale, even after years of storage. "It's a developing field, and polymers are unique — you can modify them, include additives that improve impact performance, stiffness or dimensional stability," said Edward Lucas, a mechanical engineer and polymer designer at the center. "You can add more ingredients to the cauldron and your potion will come out different, trading some characteristics for others." Several designs are in development, with inner tactical polymer containers expected to weigh about half as much as legacy steel containers. This weight savings will reduce the load on soldiers. The decrease will also be advantageous, particularly on weight-sensitive platforms such as light watercraft and aircraft. Weight affects whether these platforms can launch and plays a part in their agility. Beyond that, injection molding for these inner packs will offer supply chain advantages. More than 800 injection molders in the U.S. can likely produce these packs, creating competition, slashing costs and lowering barriers to entry for new suppliers. Additionally, polymer inner packs can be produced largely through injection molding, where most components are formed in a single custom mold and do not require large dedicated fabrication lines. Because the same press can be used for other products by swapping molds, polymer production requires a much smaller footprint and fewer dedicated tools. {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} - {{slideCaption}} Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( {{filesize}} ) Credit: {{photographer}} VIRIN: {{virin}} {{slideNumber}} of {{numSlides}} {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideTitle}} - {{slideCaption}} {{slideInfo.slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideInfo.slideTitle}} - {{slideInfo.slideCaption}} Soldiers tested the SixPAC throughout 2024-2025 and gave valuable feedback, much of it positive. Several service members pointed out that when aboard watercraft or aircraft, "every ounce counts" and that the new system will allow them to carry more ammunition. The polymer inner pack design is currently undergoing refinement, with an ongoing evaluation of options. The armaments center plans to continue investing in multiple container designs and will share pertinent information, such as performance requirements, dimensional constraints and lessons learned with industry partners. The new SixPAC system represents a critical step toward modernizing ammunition logistics and will allow the War Department to meet future challenges and demands more easily, Runell said. title: Presidential Message on Overdose and Drug Poisoning Awareness Week
text: Briefings & Statements Presidential Message on Overdose and Drug Poisoning Awareness Week The White House August 24, 2026 During Overdose and Drug Poisoning Awareness Week, our Nation renews its resolve to defeat the scourge of illicit drugs and synthetic poisons that have devastated hundreds of thousands of American lives. My Administration is relentlessly confronting this threat at every source, and we will always put our national security and the safety, health, and well-being of the American People first. When I returned to office, I vowed to stop the flow of fentanyl and other deadly drugs into our country, and my Administration immediately took action. We created the Homeland Security Task Force to bring together all federal, state and local partners to achieve the national policy goal of eliminating the cartel presence in America once and for all. By doing so, my Administration secured our southern border and began dismantling fentanyl supply chains at every link, from the narco-terrorist cartels and gangs that traffic these deadly drugs to the foreign suppliers that enable them. I proudly signed the HALT Fentanyl Act, permanently classifying fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs, ensuring dealers and traffickers will receive the maximum force of the law. I designated fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction and the worst cartels as foreign terrorist organizations, unleashing our national security resources against this attack on American soil. I have also directed military forces to conduct strikes on dozens of narcotrafficking boats to disrupt the flow of maritime supply routes. As a result, fentanyl deaths dropped 22 percent in a single year, total drug overdose deaths fell 14 percent, and thousands of American lives have been saved. The strength of our country rests upon the health of its people, and my Administration is restoring hope in every community touched by addiction. Earlier this year, I launched the Great American Recovery Initiative, uniting government, healthcare, faith communities, and the private sector behind one mission of prevention, treatment, and recovery. This program is making proven treatments more accessible, supporting Americans and families on the road to recovery, and giving every person the opportunity to build a healthy and hopeful future. This week, we remember every American lost to overdose and drug poisoning, stand with the families who carry their memory, and support all those working to overcome addiction. Above all, we vow to end the devastation wrought by deadly drugs and build a stronger, healthier, and safer America.

title: EOD Airmen Train on Full Spectrum of Explosive Threats
text: The call comes in from headquarters. "[Explosive ordnance disposal], this is Godfather. Be advised hostiles approaching your location. How copy?" Exercise Big Trouble Air Force Airman 1st Class Levi Womack, an explosive ordnance disposal technician assigned to the 341st Civil Engineer Squadron, reviews recently acquired information about a simulated chemical explosive device during Exercise Big Trouble at Limestone Hills Training Area, Mont., Aug. 18, 2026. Manipulating a device in full protective posture tests a technician's dexterity and composure. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 378.88 KB ) Credit: Air Force Tech. Sgt. Aaron Thomasson VIRIN: 260818-F-NC256-9202 Exercise Big Trouble Air Force Senior Airman Mitchell Massa, front, an explosive ordnance disposal technician assigned to the 366th Civil Engineer Squadron, and Air Force Airman 1st Class Levi Womack, an explosive ordnance disposal technician assigned to the 341st Civil Engineer Squadron, approach a simulated chemical explosive device during Exercise Big Trouble at Limestone Hills Training Area, Mont., Aug. 18, 2026. Working in chemical protective gear adds heat, restricted mobility and limited visibility, conditions technicians must train in to stay effective against contaminated threats. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 512 KB ) Credit: Air Force Tech. Sgt. Aaron Thomasson VIRIN: 260818-F-NC256-9194 Inside the gas mask, every breath feels like drinking air through a straw. Air Force Airman 1st Class Levi Womack keys the radio and responds. "Godfather, this is EOD. Good copy." Further up the ridgeline, Air Force Senior Airman Mitchell Massa hears the radio chatter and knows time is running out. He is working against the clock to disarm and decontaminate a chemical explosive device found in the woods near a forward operating base. With the seconds slipping by, his entire world narrows down to the problem in front of him, visible only through the fogged lenses of his gas mask. Then the call comes in from headquarters to leave the area. Massa works his way down the ridge, moving slowly in his chemical protective gear and drops the device in a decontamination tub. "End of scenario," yells the instructor during Exercise Big Trouble, a weeklong field training exercise at Limestone Hills Training Area near Townsend, Montana. It's only the morning of the first day and Massa and Womack are already drenched in sweat as they peel off their protective gear, hot and thirsty under the August sun. Massa, assigned to the 366th Civil Engineer Squadron at Mountain Home Air Force Base, Idaho, and Womack, assigned to the 341st Civil Engineer Squadron at Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, are there to hone their craft on simulated chemicals and explosive devices. They gather around the instructor for a debrief after finishing their second problem of the day. He tells them this scenario is meant to teach junior explosive ordnance disposal technicians what to do when external constraints make it too dangerous to continue disposal operations. Knowing when to break off a mission rather than push past the point of safety was exactly the lesson Air Force Staff Sgt. Lucky Widjaja, the exercise's main organizer and a 341st Civil Engineer Squadron EOD technician, wanted every technician to carry off the range. "The end goal is for them to realize their limitations and capabilities — the miles they're able to travel and how they function under less-than-ideal conditions," Widjaja said. "So that if that were to ever happen in a deployed environment, they have that experience to fall back on." Exercise Big Trouble Air Force Senior Airman Mitchell Massa, an explosive ordnance disposal technician assigned to the 366th Civil Engineer Squadron, operates the controls for a transportable robotic system during Exercise Big Trouble at Limestone Hills Training Area, Mont., Aug. 18, 2026. The system allows EOD teams to investigate and handle suspected devices remotely, keeping technicians outside the blast radius. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 348.16 KB ) Credit: Air Force Tech. Sgt. Aaron Thomasson VIRIN: 260818-F-NC256-9074 Exercise Big Trouble Air Force Airman 1st Class Levi Womack, right, an explosive ordnance disposal technician assigned to the 341st Civil Engineer Squadron, inspects the gas mask of Air Force Senior Airman Mitchell Massa, an explosive ordnance disposal technician assigned to the 366th Civil Engineer Squadron, during Exercise Big Trouble at Limestone Hills Training Area, Mont., Aug. 18, 2026. Confirming a proper mask seal is critical before entering a contaminated environment, where a compromised seal could expose a technician to chemical hazards. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 337.92 KB ) Credit: Air Force Tech. Sgt. Aaron Thomasson VIRIN: 260818-F-NC256-9189 Now in its fourth iteration and second year bringing in EOD airmen from around the country, this year's exercise featured six Air Force EOD teams training in a simulated deployed environment. Over the week, technicians worked though scenarios that spanned a range of threats they could see downrange, such as improvised explosive devices, unexploded ordnance, weapons caches, route denial and chemical agents, like what Massa and Womack confronted that first morning. The training plan was built for airmen early in their careers, many of them working through these high-pressure, decision-making processes for the first time. The aim was to develop technicians who understood what team leadership demanded and could transfer their skills to real-world deployed environments. If judgment, leadership and technical skill were the lessons, communication between EOD shops was the method. Planners paired technicians with counterparts from other shops to trade tactics, techniques and procedures, allowing airmen to sharpen not just their own units but the shops they trained alongside. "My favorite part is getting EOD members from different shops out here to train," Widjaja said. "It allows us to communicate and exchange learning points so that we are, as a whole EOD enterprise, more ready and capable to face our next emerging threat." Throughout the week, teams gained experience with the career field's full toolkit. Massa traded his chemical protective gear for the controls of an unmanned ground vehicle, sending the robot to examine a suspected device while the operator stayed outside the blast radius. In another case, careful planning made success possible. Air Force Staff Sgt. Hartvig Homberg, a 341st Civil Engineer Squadron EOD technician, and Air Force Airman 1st Class Jacob Miller-Lujan, a 28th Civil Engineer Squadron EOD technician from Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota, mapped out a plan before tackling a problem with multiple devices, deciding who did what and in what order. After each scenario, teams gathered to debrief, learning new lessons before moving to the next problem. The training tempo left technicians with limited recovery time. Teams woke up early to prep their gear and were on the range by 8 a.m. Once there, they rotated through problems, trading team leader and team member roles and switching between mounted and dismounted work. After a short rest at the end of the afternoon, they started a night mission brief around 9 p.m. and conducted training while using night-vision devices until at least midnight. For the airmen learning during Big Trouble, the purposeful grind of the exercise teaches not just explosives, but teamwork and endurance. "The hardest part is being tired, and keeping a good attitude and staying motivated throughout," Widjaja said. "But by the end of it, we see teams and players coming together, learning from other shops and exchanging knowledge." Experience: Military Units: Air Force

title: Navy Advances MH-60 Modernization, Identifies Industry Performers for Prototype Project
text: Flare Deployment An MH-60R Sea Hawk assigned to Helicopter Maritime Strike Squadron 77, embarked on the aircraft carrier USS George Washington, deploys flares during a strike coordination and reconnaissance exercise while operating in the South China Sea, Aug. 12, 2026. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 788.48 KB ) Credit: Navy Seaman Anthony Vilardi VIRIN: 260812-N-VQ739-8020 In a critical step to ensure long-term fleet readiness and secure dominance in the maritime domain, the Navy's MH-60 Sea Hawk helicopter service life modernization program recently announced the industry performers identified to proceed to the first phase of a statement of work collaboration for the MH-60 tailorable architecture leveraging open systems prototype project. Led by the H-60 Multi-Mission Helicopter program office, in a joint cooperative effort with the Royal Australian Navy, the prototype project will simultaneously modernize the MH-60 avionics and mission system architecture while resolving multiple obsolescence issues. The project is designed to deliver a cost-effective platform that can rapidly respond to emerging threats, adapt to new fleet requirements and support MH-60 sustainment through the 2050 timeframe. Through collaborative digital engineering and open-system design, this joint effort strengthens U.S. and allied maritime forces' ability to outpace emerging global threats for decades to come. To execute this modernization strategy, the government is using another transaction authority agreement facilitated by the Naval Aviation Systems Consortium to engage industry partners across three critical roles: Lead aircraft integrator: Sierra Nevada Corp was identified to design the physical and structural integration for the MH-60S variant. Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems was identified to design the physical and structural integration for the MH-60R variant. Segment lead integrator-flight critical avionics segment: Rockwell Collins Inc., and Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems were identified as the segment lead integrators responsible for hardware and software architecture design, interface management, and system-level software integration for the flight critical avionics segment and the digital backbone system. Open system verification demonstration third-party integrator: Technology Security Associates Inc., was identified to support the government's assessment of how segment integrators implement a modular open systems approach in the flight critical avionics segment and the digital backbone system, including open system verification demonstrations. {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} - {{slideCaption}} Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( {{filesize}} ) Credit: {{photographer}} VIRIN: {{virin}} {{slideNumber}} of {{numSlides}} {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideTitle}} - {{slideCaption}} {{slideInfo.slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideInfo.slideTitle}} - {{slideInfo.slideCaption}} This does not constitute formal contract or agreement awards, which remain contingent upon successful negotiation and finalization of the Phase 1 statements of work, laying the groundwork for a major leap in naval aviation technology and marking a critical step toward potential prototype development for the flight critical avionics segment and the digital backbone system. Under this phased acquisition approach, Phase 1 will focus on the preliminary fight critical avionics segment and the digital backbone system design, establishing the collaborative digital engineering environment and characterizing the baseline aircraft through physical integration, structural modification, A-kit fabrication, and preparation for aircraft-level testing. Phase 2 will focus on prototype development and verification activities. By using modern digital acquisition practices and modular open systems approach standards, the prototype project will support MH-60 Sea Hawk key business drivers while also streamlining future vertical lift development with portable open core architecture. The MH-60R specializes in antisubmarine warfare, surface warfare, electronic warfare, and command and control. The MH-60S is used for performing antisurface warfare, combat search and rescue, special warfare support and airborne mine countermeasures.

title: Exercise Northern Viking Marks 75 Years of Defense Cooperation
text: U.S. service members arrived in Keflavik, Iceland, yesterday, joining forces with the Icelandic Coast Guard and other NATO allies for the U.S. 6th Fleet's Exercise Northern Viking 2026. Northern Viking Air Force Gen. Alexus G. Grynkewich, NATO supreme allied commander Europe and commander of U.S. European Command, delivers remarks during the opening ceremony of Exercise Northern Viking 26 at Keflavik Air Base, Iceland, Aug. 18, 2026. The exercise strengthens interoperability and force readiness between the U.S., Iceland and allied nations. Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( 3.25 MB ) Credit: Navy Chief Petty Officer Justin Stumberg VIRIN: 260818-N-XT273-1006 Participating nations include Belgium, Denmark, France, Iceland, Norway, Poland and the U.S., alongside specialized assets and personnel assigned to the Allied Maritime Command and NATO Joint Force Command Norfolk. "Our defense cooperation with the United States has thrived for 75 years because it has never stood still; it has developed to meet [the] evolving challenges of our time," said Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir, Iceland's minister for foreign affairs, during the exercise's opening ceremony. "The best way to celebrate this anniversary is not merely by commemorating our partnership, but by actually practicing it — together and alongside our allies. Northern Viking is precisely that, a demonstration that the commitments we have made to one another are dynamic, practical and built on trust, underpinned by shared interests." This year's iteration of the biennial exercise marks the 75th anniversary of the 1951 bilateral defense agreement between Iceland and the U.S. Running from Aug. 22 to Sept. 3, Northern Viking will challenge joint and coalition forces with a series of highly realistic training scenarios. Key training opportunities will focus on antisubmarine warfare, mine countermeasures, expeditionary construction, search and rescue, humanitarian medical response and disaster response. Opening Remarks Air Force Gen. Alexus G. Grynkewich, NATO supreme allied commander Europe and commander of U.S. European Command, delivers remarks during the opening ceremony of Exercise Northern Viking 26 at Keflavik Air Base, Iceland, Aug. 18, 2026. J. T. Anderson, U.S. 6th Fleet commander. "Northern Viking 2026 is a demonstration of our commitment to the collective defense of the North Atlantic. Together with our allies, we continue to create an environment that allows interoperability among NATO maritime forces so that European allies can take over primary responsibility for deterrence and defense in the European theater." Exercise Northern Viking 2026 is designed to strengthen interoperability and force readiness between the U.S., Iceland and other allied nations. The exercise enables critical multidomain command and control of joint and coalition forces defending Iceland and safeguarding the sea lines of communication within the waterways between Greenland, Iceland and the United Kingdom. As a vital global shipping corridor, keeping this area secure is an imperative for transatlantic trade, commerce and security between North America and Europe. "Together, we're honing our warfighting skills and ensuring our ability to secure this critical region and to project decisive combat power wherever and whenever necessary," said Air Force Gen Alexus G. Grynkewich, NATO supreme allied commander Europe and commander of U.S. European Command. "Throughout this exercise, and others, we will leverage the power of data in [artificial intelligence] enabled decision support tools, will integrate data streams in real time and ensure our command and control structures can make decisions at the speed of future conflict." {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} - {{slideCaption}} Share: × Share Copy Link Email Facebook X LinkedIn WhatsApp Download: Full Size ( {{filesize}} ) Credit: {{photographer}} VIRIN: {{virin}} {{slideNumber}} of {{numSlides}} {{slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideTitle}} - {{slideCaption}} {{slideInfo.slideNumber}}/{{numSlides}} {{slideInfo.slideTitle}} - {{slideInfo.slideCaption}} The 1951 defense agreement was the foundation of a unique security framework designating the U.S. as responsible for Iceland's defense in the absence of its own standing military. Over the last 75 years, this partnership has adapted from Cold War deterrence to modern multidomain defense operations, ensuring that the transatlantic bridge remains open and secure.
